Then dropped the body into the surf.

Dead.

Second Covenant name finished.

Blood at his mouth.

Waves around his boots.

“You killed him.”

“My blood is smarter than his research.”

“That sounded arrogant.”

“What now?”

Keira Morn.

Not danger.

Urgency.

Drakonis.

A face.

Not Dren.

Not Mara.

Keira Morn.

“Of course.”

The world was making this efficient.

Chapter Seventy-Three

High Witch Keira Morn

Keira Morn attacked Drakonis because she thought Zee would not arrive in time.

She was correct.

Zee did not.

Zareth handled her first.

By the time Zee and Ner reached the mountain kingdom, half of Keira’s strike force was already dead.

The other half wished they were.

Zareth had trapped them inside a volcanic pass.

Not with magic.

With geography.

One collapsed ridge behind.

Dragonfire ahead.

No escape.

Rez would have approved.

Zee landed at the lower path—

without wings.

Fast.

Blood on his teeth.

Teal-and-Gold fire leaking between them.

Anger.

Pride.

Above.

High Witch.

Powerful.

Calm.

Zee barely reacted.

Zareth.

Ner.

Drakonis soldiers.

His people elsewhere.

Difference.

The mountain lit.

Dragon suppression.

Slits.

Good.

Zee folded the paper.

His pupils became human again.

Calm.

Thinking.

He had killed Mara before another strike.

Dren before another experiment.

Zareth had killed Keira after Drakonis was attacked.

Each line different.

Each choice moving.

Now Caldus intended something broader than one kingdom.

Bloodlines.

Entire categories of people.

Zee looked west.

“Salt cathedral.”

Ner nodded.

“When?”

Zee thought.

For once, not immediately.

“After we know what it is.”

Ner smiled faintly.

“Growth.”

Zee looked at him.

“No.”

Then his eyes shifted into slits.

“Preparation.”

Far below, Zareth roared across Drakonis.

The sound carried through mountain valleys.

Not fear.

Warning.

And somewhere beyond the western flats, a man called Father Caldus was preparing to erase bloodlines he believed should never have existed.

He had not attacked Zee directly yet.

That was becoming less relevant.

Because King Zee Darkheart had finally reached the point where evidence of intended extermination was enough.

He was no longer waiting for the first body.

Chapter Seventy-Four

The Salt Cathedral

The western salt flats had no roads.

Only white.

Miles of cracked earth reflecting sunlight hard enough to hurt ordinary eyes.

Zee walked through it without squinting.

Ner beside him.

Rez had rejoined them at the border after Vesper’s aqueduct threat was contained.

Zareth arrived in human form.

That was still new enough that Rez stared.

Zareth noticed.

“If you keep looking at me like that, I am shifting back.”

Rez blinked.

“You talk more than I expected.”

Zareth’s expression went flat.

“I have always had opinions.”

Zee smiled.

“Unfortunately.”

Zareth looked toward him.

Through the Link:

You missed this.

Zee answered privately.

A little.

Warmth came back beneath the words.

Then smoke.

Drakonis.

Damage still under repair.

Responsibility waiting.

Zareth had come because Father Caldus threatened mixed bloodlines across kingdoms, including Veyrath and potentially Drakonis alliances.

Not because Zee summoned him.

Good.

The salt cathedral appeared near noon.

No towers.

No walls.

It had been carved downward.

A massive open pit cut into the flats, white stone descending in terraces toward a dark sanctuary beneath the earth.

Rez looked over the edge.

“I hate stairs.”

Ner glanced down.

“There are hundreds.”

“I hate them more now.”

Zareth smiled.

“You have legs.”

Rez stared.

“You had wings for most of your life.”

“Still do.”

“Exactly.”

Zee started down.

“Argue later.”

⸻

Nobody attacked them.

That was suspicious.

The first chamber contained no guards.

The second held candles.

The third held names.

Hundreds.

Painted across salt walls.

Zee stopped.

Wolf.

Witch.

Vampire.

Dragon-Witch.

Mixed blood.

Unknown blood.

Bloodsong.

Tribrid.

Ner went very still.

His name was there.

NEREUS AZRION.

Zareth found another.

AURELIA VEYRATH.

Dead.

Still listed.

Then:

THERON VEYRATH.

SERAPHINE VEYRATH.

Rez found his own.

Not because mixed.

Because proximity.

REZ VESPER — ENABLER.

He frowned.

“I am offended by how boring mine is.”

Ner looked toward Zee’s section.

His name occupied an entire column.

ZEE DARKHEART.

Below it:

PRIMARY CONVERGENCE THREAT.

ADAPTIVE BLOOD.

UNSTABLE SPECIES BOUNDARY.

DIVINE-KILLING CAPACITY CONFIRMED.

CRIMSON DRAGON MUTATION.

Zee’s pupils narrowed.

“Very dramatic.”

Zareth folded his arms.

“You are one to talk.”

Zee looked at him.

“You have become irritating in human form.”

“I had to compensate for twenty-one years of you translating me badly.”

Rez laughed.

Ner actually stopped reading to look between them.

Zee pointed.

“I never translated you badly.”

Through the Link, Zareth sent Zee an old childhood memory.

Zee telling someone Zareth had said hello.

What Zareth had actually felt was suspicion, hunger, and a desire to bite the roof.

Zee frowned.

“That was close enough.”

“Liar.”

Good.

The humor lasted four seconds.

Then Ner touched the wall.

Pure Golden Mana spread.

His expression changed.

“These names are recent.”

“How recent?” Rez asked.

“Some days.”

Zee looked down the corridor.

“Caldus is here.”

“No,” Ner said.

Silence.

He studied the structure again.

“These walls are receiving information.”

Rez’s hand moved to his sword.

“From where?”

“I don’t know.”

Zee listened.

No heartbeat beneath them.

No blood.

No obvious living presence.

Zareth’s Dragon senses sharpened.

Then he spoke aloud.

“There is something lower.”

Zee looked toward him.

“What?”

Zareth’s eyes narrowed.

“Not someone.”

Through the Link came more.

Heat without fire.

A pressure beneath the salt.

Something old, but not divine.

Not friendly.

Not awake.

Zee felt the sensory layer beneath Zareth’s words.

Deep vibration.

Mineral.

Bone?

No.

Something structural.

Ner stepped away from the wall.

“The cathedral is built on something.”

Rez sighed.

“Of course it is.”

⸻

They found Father Caldus in the lowest chamber.

Alone.

Old.

Human.

No supernatural blood.

No armor.

No guards.

He sat at a stone table surrounded by paper.

He looked up when they entered.

“King Darkheart.”

Zee stopped.

“Father Caldus.”

Caldus looked toward Ner.

Then Rez.

Then Zareth.

His gaze lingered.

“Crown Prince Drakonis. Human form suits diplomacy.”

Zareth’s voice went colder.

“You cut Dragon bloodlines into categories.”

Caldus smiled.

“I classify risk.”

“You classify people you intend to erase.”

“Yes.”

No denial.

Rez looked disgusted.

“That saves time.”

Caldus folded his hands.

“I wondered which of you would say it first.”

Zee walked closer.

“Where are the kill orders?”

“Already distributed.”

Ner’s Gold flared.

Rez moved.

Zareth’s eyes sharpened.

Zee did not.

Calm.

“Targets?”

Caldus smiled.

“All over.”

Zee heard the heartbeat.

Steady.

No bluff.

Bad.

“How many?”

“Forty-three bloodlines.”

“Active strikes?”

“Seven.”

Rez swore.

Zareth’s voice dropped into something closer to Dragon thunder even in human shape.

“Drakonis?”

“One.”

“Ner?”

“One.”

“Veyrath?”

“Two.”

Zee’s pupils became slits.

“And Darkheart?”

Caldus smiled.

“Not the House.”

“You.”

Silence.

Zee looked at him.

“Where?”

“You are already here.”

That was the trap.

Ner realized first.

“Zee.”

The salt beneath them lit.

Not Witchcraft.

Something else.

Caldus stood.

“I could never overpower you.”

“No.”

“So I built a place that does not need to.”

The floor split.

Not downward.

Inward.

White salt opened into a black mineral chamber far beneath the cathedral.

Zareth’s voice sharpened.

“Move!”

Too late.

The entire sanctuary dropped.

⸻

They fell into darkness.

Zareth shifted midair.

Human body exploded outward into true Dragon form.

Wings opened.

Massive.

He caught Rez with one foreclaw.

Ner with the other.

Zee did not need catching.

He hit the sloped wall, claws digging in, slid twenty feet, then pushed off.

Dragon durability absorbed the rest.

He landed hard.

Caldus landed on a suspended platform above.

Protected by mechanisms.

Zee looked up.

“You planned that.”

“Yes.”

“I respect preparation.”

Caldus stared.

“That is not the response I wanted.”

Zee smiled.

Then the chamber woke.

Something moved beneath the salt.

Not a creature.

A network.

Black crystal roots spread through the cavern.

Every supernatural nature reacted differently.

Ner’s Gold flickered.

Rez’s Blue-White Mana weakened.

Zareth’s Dragonfire dimmed.

Zee felt all four natures strain.

Not suppression.

Separation.

The chamber was trying to make each supernatural force exist alone.

Zee’s Witch nature pulled away from Vampire.

Wolf from Dragon.

Not physically.

Structurally.

Caldus looked down.

“This is what the world should have remained.”

Zee’s face went cold.

“Separate.”

“Yes.”

Ner gritted his teeth.

“You built a weapon out of a natural formation.”

Caldus smiled.

“Finally.”

Rez looked around.

“Can it be broken?”

Ner studied.

“Not quickly.”

Zareth spoke through the Link while also growling aloud.

Three anchors. North wall. Under platform. Beneath us.

Zee received more than words.

Heat.

Positions.

A weak pulse under the salt.

He answered instantly.

Take the north. Rez gets the platform. Ner finds the lower anchor. I take Caldus.

Zareth’s mental reply came with irritation.

You always take the person.

He talks too much.

A wave of Dragon amusement broke through the strain.

Then they moved.

The adult Link made them terrifying.

No shouted explanation.

No delay.

Zareth blasted the north wall.

Rez used the opening to climb toward the platform.

Ner drove Gold into the floor in hair-thin lines.

Zee ran straight up the salt column.

Caldus saw him.

Panic finally entered his heartbeat.

Good.

Zee reached the platform.

Caldus triggered another mechanism.

Iron spikes fired.

Zee barely turned his wrist.

Silent magic.

The spikes shifted around him.

One embedded beside Caldus’s head.

Zee continued walking.

Caldus backed up.

“You are destabilizing everything.”

“Yes.”

“You could collapse the chamber.”

“Yes.”

“And kill us all.”

Zee smiled faintly.

“You keep forgetting.”

Caldus’s face changed.

Right.

Zee could not die.

Caldus could.

“Stop.”

“No.”

Zee crossed the last distance.

Caldus raised a poison blade.

Nanda Parbat read the shoulder.

Zee caught his wrist before the blade cleared cloth.

Twist.

Break.

Caldus screamed.

Zee’s smile vanished.

“Where are the seven strikes?”

Caldus spat blood.

“Too late.”

Vampire compulsion hit.

“Where?”

Caldus resisted.

Ordinary Human.

Extraordinary discipline.

Zee pushed harder.

“Tell me.”

The man shook violently.

Then laughed.

“Even if I tell you, you cannot reach them all.”

Zee looked toward Zareth.

The Link opened.

Not words first.

Drakonis.

Distance.

Air routes.

Then speech.

I can reach one.

Rez shouted from below.

“Vesper can reach another if we send now!”

Ner looked up.

“Veyrath survivors are scattered. We can warn both.”

Zee returned to Caldus.

“You were saying?”

Fear.

Good.

“Locations.”

Compulsion broke him.

Seven places.

Fast.

Specific.

Rez memorized.

Ner sent Golden signal marks through prepared communication charms.

Zareth’s Link carried one thought before he shifted toward flight.

I am taking Drakonis.

Zee answered.

Go.

No ownership.

No request to stay.

Zareth launched upward through the broken chamber.

Caldus watched.

His plan collapsing faster than he could process.

Zee leaned close.

“You chose bloodlines before they acted.”

Caldus glared.

“They would have.”

“Some.”

“Yes.”

“Not all.”

“Eventually.”

There it was.

Possibility as guilt.

Victor again.

Zee was tired of it.

He killed Caldus quickly.

One hand.

Neck.

No feeding.

He did not want the blood.

Caldus dropped.

The last principal name was finished.

Then the floor cracked.

Ner shouted.

“Zee!”

The chamber began collapsing.

Permanent progress had arrived.

Now survival.

Good.

Zee jumped.

⸻

They escaped through the upper shaft as the salt cathedral imploded behind them.

Rez emerged coughing.

Ner covered in white dust.

Zee barely singed.

Zareth already gone toward Drakonis.

Through the Link:

Still alive.

Zee answered.

Disappointing.

Zareth’s laughter came through with mountain wind and urgency.

Then he was gone.

Rez looked toward the horizon.

“Seven attacks.”

Ner nodded.

“Now six.”

Zee looked at him.

“How?”

Ner smiled faintly.

“Bloodsong warning reached one Veyrath enclave before the strike landed.”

Good.

Rez drew breath.

“Vesper will handle ours.”

“Drakonis handles theirs.”

Zee’s eyes narrowed.

“And the others?”

Ner looked toward him.

“Darkheart has people.”

Zee understood.

Not everything required him personally.

King.

Network.

Influence.

He turned east.

“Then we move.”

The Covenant’s Five were finished.

But Caldus had already thrown seven knives into the world.

Now the question was not whether Zee could stop them all himself.

It was whether the world had finally learned something worse.

King Zee Darkheart was no longer one predator.

He had people who moved when he did.

And they were getting faster.

Chapter Seventy-Five

Seven Knives

The attacks landed within three hours.

None looked the same.

That was what made them dangerous.

Vesper’s was sabotage.

Drakonis faced a direct strike.

One Veyrath enclave received poisoned rain.

A mixed-blood settlement east of Darkheart was attacked by hired Wolves.

A coastal Bloodsong rumor-cell was targeted by Vampire killers who thought Ner had created more like himself.

Wrong.

There was only Ner.

Another strike hit a Demon-Witch refuge under neutral protection.

The last came for Zee.

That one waited until he returned to Darkheart.

Of course.

⸻

Rez’s message arrived first.

Aqueduct secure. Four dead. Nine captured. Father furious. I am enjoying it.

Zee smiled.

Ner read over his shoulder.

“He wrote that?”

“Yes.”

“That is concerning.”

“No.”

“Why?”

“Lucien furious is apparently entertaining.”

Ner looked unconvinced.

Then his own Bloodsong pulsed.

He stopped.

“Veyrath.”

Zee’s face changed.

“What?”

“Someone is bleeding.”

“Who?”

Ner closed his eyes.

His Bloodsong had learned distance imperfectly over the years.

Not names.

Not thoughts.

Resonance.

Blood he had encountered before was easier.

Theron.

Zee smelled Ner’s fear before he spoke.

“Theron.”

Zee’s hand closed.

Then the Link hit.

Zareth.

Full sentence.

Drakonis is under control. Do not come here. Go to Theron.

Beneath it Zee felt torn wing membrane, smoke, two broken talons, and Zareth lying about how fine he was.

Zee answered privately.

You are bleeding.

I said under control, not comfortable.

Idiot.

Go.

Zee went.

⸻

Theron had already killed three attackers when Zee arrived.

Seraphine killed the fourth.

Good.

No helpless family.

Theron leaned against a stone wall with poison spreading black beneath one Dragon scale patch.

Seraphine stood over a dead Witch.

“You are late.”

Zee crouched beside Theron.

“You are alive.”

“Barely.”

“Dramatic.”

Theron smiled weakly.

“Family trait.”

Ner arrived seconds later and dropped beside him.

Pure Gold formed.

Bloodsong followed.

The poison reacted badly.

Ner frowned.

“This was designed for Veyrath.”

Zee smelled it.

Dragonbane.

Witch suppression.

Blood clotting agent.

Specialized.

His body recognized pieces.

Not whole.

He opened his palm with one claw.

Seraphine immediately said:

“No.”

Zee looked at her.

“One drop.”

“You do not know what that does.”

“Neither do you.”

“That is why I said no.”

Theron coughed.

“I vote yes.”

Seraphine glared.

“You are poisoned.”

“Exactly. Motivated reasoning.”

Zee almost laughed.

Then seriousness returned.

He placed one drop of Crimson blood against the poison near Theron’s wound.

Ner isolated it with Gold.

The reaction was immediate.

The black spread stopped.

Not cured.

Stopped.

Zee’s accumulated resistance interfered with the poison’s structure.

Ner used Bloodsong to push the broken toxin away from Theron’s heart.

Seraphine added Witchcraft.

Three powers.

Not one solution.

Theron breathed easier.

Zee looked at Ner.

“Can you finish?”

“Yes.”

Good.

Zee stood.

One attacker remained alive.

Seraphine had kept him that way deliberately.

The man knelt against a pillar.

Human.

Terrified.

The attacker whispered:

“Please.”

“Caldus.”

“Directly?”

“Yes.”

Truth.

“Anyone else involved?”

“No.”

Truth.

“Did you know who lived here?”

“Yes.”

“Did you know there were children?”

The man froze.

Seraphine’s face hardened.

Zee smelled the answer.

“Yes.”

He killed him.

Quick.

No speech.

No guilt.

Then turned back to Theron.

Different.

Gentler.

Both Zee.

Theron watched him.

“Aurelia would worry about you.”

Zee stopped.

Not because the name was forbidden.

Because Theron had earned the right to use it.

“I know.”

“She would also be glad I am alive.”

“Yes.”

“Then focus on that.”

Zee looked at him.

For one second, human pupils.

Then he nodded.

No moral reset.

Just family.

⸻

The mixed-blood settlement survived because Darkheart riders arrived before Zee.

That mattered.

His people were learning.

The coastal Vampire strike failed because Ner sent a Bloodsong warning through three connected blood samples before the killers reached shore.

That frightened him.

Not because the power was bad.

Because it was growing.

He told Zee later.

“I could feel them before they arrived.”

“How far?”

“Too far.”

“That is not a measurement.”

“I know.”

Zee smiled.

Ner did not.

Zee touched his face.

“What?”

Ner looked at him.

“If I can reach blood from that far away eventually…”

“Yes.”

“What stops me from touching everyone?”

Zee’s expression softened.

“You.”

Ner stared.

Not because Zee was calling him good.

Because the answer placed responsibility where it belonged.

Ner nodded.

“Fair.”

Then kissed him.

Brief.

Needed.

The moment ended when a Darkheart horn sounded.

Attack seven.

Home.

⸻

The killers came through the throne hall.

Four.

Not an army.

Professionals.

They knew Zee’s patrol schedule.

They knew the hidden stair.

They knew the old Victor-era passages.

One had been a Darkheart servant years ago.

Betrayal.

Different category.

Zee entered silently behind them.

The first assassin never knew.

Knife.

Down.

Second turned.

Vampire.

He saw Zee’s eyes.

Slits.

Tried compulsion.

Zee smiled.

“Really?”

The command broke against him.

Zee answered.

“Kneel.”

The Vampire resisted.

Strong.

Older than Zee.

Did not matter enough.

Vampire dominance pressed through voice and blood.

The attacker’s knees hit stone.

Third and fourth moved together.

Witch and Wolf.

Good coordination.

The Witch’s spell veered left.

The Wolf adjusted.

Exactly what Zee expected.

Nanda Parbat.

He stepped into the new line.

One elbow.

One broken wrist.

Wolf claws caught his shoulder.

Crimson-black scales took most of it.

Headbutt.

Horn edge opened blood.

Wolf Zee without transforming.

Natural.

Complete.

Her spell structure collapsed.

Not compulsion.

Witchcraft.

Precise.

Interesting.

No eye contact.

The Wolf on the floor smelled terrified.

Zee liked that.

Then the former Darkheart servant—the first assassin he thought was down—moved.

Not dead.

Feigning.

Good technique.

Bad luck.

Caught the hand.

The servant stared.

“You remember me.”

Zee remembered everyone who had worked near Aurelia.

This man had served wine at two dinners.

Opened doors.

Carried letters.

“You destroyed the House.”

Darkheart banners.

Living guards.

People choosing loyalty instead of inherited fear.

“No.”

Personal.

Not Caldus.

Not bloodline philosophy.

Grief.

Fight.

Victor loyalists.

Recognition.

Darkheart guards.

Servants.

“Your grief is yours.”

“What you do with it is also yours.”

Personal.

Fast.

No feeding.

Zee spared two.

Fully.

Because he wanted the blood.

No apology.

⸻

By midnight, all seven attacks had failed.

Not without losses.

Nine dead across four territories.

Twenty-three wounded.

Theron alive.

Zareth alive.

Lucien alive.

Veyrath survivors still standing.

Mixed-blood settlements damaged but not destroyed.

None reached the heart.

Zee sat on the Darkheart throne after the reports ended.

Rez appeared through a communication mirror from Vesper.

My wing is fine.

Liar.

Almost.

“Majesty.”

Reputation.

Prevention.

You like that they were afraid.

Good.

Good?

Useful.

Bloodsong.

Crimson-and-gold eyes calm.

Human pupils.

For now.

At twenty-one, he was beginning to understand its most useful form.

Not panic.

Not cruelty.

Deterrence.

And King Zee Darkheart had every intention of learning how far it could reach.

Chapter Seventy-Six

The Attack That Never Happened

No alarm sounded.

No village burned.

No assassin entered Darkheart.

Nobody was poisoned.

That was why the report mattered.

Lord Merek placed one folded letter on Zee’s table.

“Intercepted at the southern border.”

Zee opened it.

Rez leaned over one shoulder.

Ner sat across from him.

“You became annoying the moment you got a throne.”

Create a code for this “YES. That’s the next real escalation. 🔥

We should stop treating 21 like a permanent present-day age. Zee is immortal in the sense that he cannot permanently die, but that does not mean the story freezes him at twenty-one. Time keeps moving. Zee keeps getting older. Zareth, Ner, and Rez keep getting older too. Twenty-one is just where we are right now.

So after Chapter 75, I’d start letting years move naturally again. Not necessarily giant jumps every chapter, but enough that the book feels like we are actually watching Zee’s life, not one year stretched across hundreds of chapters.

He can become 22.

And keep going.

His face/body can mature with age instead of being frozen forever. His supernatural nature can slow or alter aging later if we ever want that, but right now there is no reason to lock him at twenty-one.

And the bigger thing:

It is finally time for Zee to create hybrids.

Not because Zee wakes up and thinks:

“I wonder what my blood can make.”

That would be too random.

The world needs to force him into it.

The attacks keep coming.

Different kingdoms.

Different supernatural species.

Assassins.

Poisons.

Sieges.

Blood weapons.

Magic.

Creatures.

People attacking villages.

People attacking children.

People attacking Darkheart citizens specifically because they chose Zee.

At first Zee keeps saving them himself.

Then Darkheart soldiers get stronger.

Then his witches improve.

Then his Wolves.

Then Vampires.

But eventually Zee hits a situation where ordinary supernatural people simply cannot survive what is coming.

That is when the hybrid creation becomes emotional.

Imagine a major attack where Darkheart is being overwhelmed.

A Witch Zee cares about is dying.

A Vampire is dying beside them.

A Wolf is torn apart protecting civilians.

Zee can save people individually, but he cannot be everywhere.

And then Zee realizes something Ner already proved years earlier:

His blood can preserve one supernatural nature while adding another.

Ner was the accident.

Now Zee finally understands the implication.

That’s when he makes the choice deliberately.

Create an army.

At first:

Save this person.

That person wakes up changed.

And Zee realizes:

Oh.

😭🔥

Witch–Vampire

Later a completely different event forces:

Vampire–Wolf

Wolf–Witch

That makes each original hybrid creation matter historically.

And every one should begin with a person, not a race name.

Someone Zee knows.

Someone dying.

Someone he chooses to save.

Then the world eventually realizes:

Zee Darkheart can create new supernatural bloodlines.

THAT is when the endless attacks can get even worse. 😭

Because suddenly Zee isn’t only dangerous because of what he is.

Now kingdoms realize he can change what other people are.

And that creates a perfect vicious cycle:

The world attacks Zee because it fears him.

Zee needs stronger people to protect Darkheart.

Zee creates hybrids to keep his people alive.

The world sees the hybrids.

The world becomes even more afraid.

They attack harder.

Zee evolves.

His hybrids become stronger.

More people choose Darkheart because it becomes one of the few places where mixed supernatural people can survive.

Darkheart grows.

The world panics more.

Attack → adaptation → growth → fear → bigger attack → more adaptation.

That is basically the prophecy becoming a civilization-level problem now.

His kingdom starts becoming something fundamentally different under him.

Not because he announces:

“I will build a supernatural empire.”

It happens because people keep coming to him for protection.

Witches.

Vampires.

Wolves.

Mixed blood.

Outcasts.

People kingdoms want dead.

And Zee keeps saying:

Come here.

Then somebody attacks them.

And Zee kills the attacker. 😭

One thing I really want to protect, though: the hybrids shouldn’t instantly become disposable soldiers.

The first ones should feel historic and personal.

Zee is creating people, not weapons.

They can fight for him.

They can defend Darkheart.

But they should have personalities, families, wants, disagreements, and their own reasons for choosing Zee.

That fits Zee much better because he hates ownership.

So the next era of the story becomes:

Zee aging.

The endless attacks getting worse.

Darkheart expanding.

Zee realizing he cannot personally protect everyone.

The first deliberate hybrid creation.

Then the world discovering that the First Natural Tribrid can create supernatural bloodlines of his own.

Yeah.

That’s where we go now. 😌🩸🔥”

Chapter Seventy-Six

The People Zee Could Not Reach

Winter reached Darkheart three months after the Covenant fell.

Zee turned twenty-two beneath a sky full of snow.

He did not celebrate much.

Darkheart did.

That was different.

The old Witch kingdom had changed around him.

Mixed-blood families crossed the gates without hiding what they were.

Again.

Calm.

Cold.

A dying Witch had survived.

Now he possessed fangs.

Vampire strength.

Vampire hunger.

And all of his Witchcraft.

The world had spent twenty-two years fearing what Zee Darkheart was.

Now it had something new to fear.

What his blood could make.

Chapter Seventy-Eight

The First Hybrid

By spring, Darkheart had stopped calling Kael Marrin an accident.

Not because anyone understood him completely.

Because he had survived long enough to become undeniable.

His Witchcraft remained intact.

His Vampire nature remained stable.

He could cast without weakening his healing.

Feed without losing magic.

Use Vampire speed while shaping Witch sigils.

Compel weak minds.

Sense blood.

Heal wounds that would once have ended his career.

That mattered to Kael more.

“You owe me seventeen silver.”

“You cheated.”

Good.

Different normal.

Human pupils.

“Understandable.”

Kael looked at him.

“You have a name.”

Ner frowned.

“Several, unfortunately.”

“Bloodsong stuck.”

“Yes.”

Kael folded his arms.

“So what am I?”

Zee leaned back.

“Kael.”

Kael gave him a look.

“We established that.”

Ner laughed.

Zee smiled.

Then became serious.

“Witch.”

“Yes.”

“Vampire.”

“Yes.”

“No third bloodline.”

“No.”

“No loss of either.”

“No.”

Zee shrugged.

“Witch-Vampire.”

Kael stared.

“That simple?”

Merek said, “Most historical names start simple.”

Kael considered.

“Witch-Vampire.”

Ner nodded.

“Accurate.”

Elara smiled.

“Terrible for poetry.”

Kael looked toward Zee.

“Fine.”

And just like that, history acquired a name.

Not through prophecy.

Not divine declaration.

Not a glowing sign in the sky.

A soldier wanted people to stop describing him like an experiment.

The first Witch-Vampire stood inside Darkheart and chose the words for what he had become.

⸻

The world reacted within a month.

Letters came.

Some peaceful.

Some terrified.

One kingdom requested formal assurances Zee would not transform foreign citizens.

Another offered gold for “controlled access” to his blood.

One threatened sanctions.

One offered an alliance.

A Vampire court asked whether Witch-Vampires could reproduce naturally.

Zee had no idea.

He burned that letter mostly because the wording annoyed him.

Then came the worst one.

A declaration from three minor Houses.

They demanded Darkheart cease “unnatural bloodline manufacturing.”

Zee read it twice.

Then handed it to Ner.

Ner read.

Looked toward Kael training in the courtyard below.

“He thinks you manufactured him.”

Zee’s expression darkened.

“They all do.”

“No.”

Ner folded the letter.

“Some know better.”

Zee looked at him.

“Doesn’t matter.”

“It does.”

“Why?”

“Because fear spreading is not the same as everyone believing the same thing.”

Fair.

Zee hated when Ner made distinctions during good anger.

Still useful.

Zee looked out over Darkheart.

New homes.

New training yards.

Witch wards beside Vampire night patrols.

Wolf sentries running forest edges.

Refugees becoming citizens.

Kael teaching two guards how to fight around enhanced Vampire speed without depending on it.

Darkheart was changing.

Not because Zee announced an empire.

Because people kept arriving.

And stayed.

Zee looked at the declaration again.

His pupils narrowed.

“The world thinks I’m building monsters.”

Ner stood beside him.

“Are you?”

Zee looked toward Kael.

“No.”

Then toward the refugee district.

“I’m building somewhere they can survive.”

That difference mattered.

The world might not care.

Darkheart would.

⸻

Chapter Seventy-Nine

The Wolf Who Refused to Die

Summer came with war.

Not a grand one.

A border war.

Those were sometimes worse.

The Kingdom of Brann wanted three miles of Darkheart forest and the iron beneath it.

Nothing mystical.

Nothing prophetic.

Land.

Money.

Power.

They invaded with soldiers, Wolves, and Witch artillery.

Darkheart pushed them back.

Brann returned with silver.

Darkheart adapted.

Brann returned with fire.

Darkheart reinforced.

Then Brann learned about Kael.

The third assault carried weapons built specifically for hybrid bodies.

They did not know enough to make them effective.

They killed ordinary defenders instead.

That was worse.

⸻

Zee reached the southern ridge halfway through the battle.

Too late for the first line.

Again.

Nine Darkheart soldiers already dead.

Seventeen wounded.

Kael fought among them.

Witch sigils flashed from one hand.

Vampire speed carried him between soldiers.

He caught a silver-tipped spear through the side.

Snapped the shaft.

Kept moving.

Alive.

Harder to kill.

Exactly what Zee wanted.

Then Zee smelled someone else.

Vampire.

Darkheart.

Dying.

He found her beneath a collapsed barricade.

Her name was Tessa Vale.

Twenty-eight.

Vampire for eleven years.

Former traveling healer before turning.

Joined Darkheart after her old Vampire nest demanded she feed from unwilling humans.

She refused.

They broke both her hands.

Zee’s people found her half-dead on a road two years earlier.

Tessa stayed.

She learned battlefield medicine.

Never became a great fighter.

Did not want to.

She saved people instead.

Today she had pulled four soldiers out of Witchfire before the ridge collapsed on her.

One leg was crushed.

Half her chest burned.

Worse—

a Wolf weapon had torn through her abdomen.

Not ordinary claws.

A curse-treated blade carrying concentrated Wolf venom designed to overwhelm Vampire healing.

Tessa’s regeneration had stopped.

Zee lifted the stone from her.

She opened one eye.

“King.”

“Don’t talk.”

“That bad?”

“Yes.”

“Wonderful.”

He almost smiled.

Then she coughed.

Blood.

Vampire.

Old healing energy failing.

A Darkheart medic knelt.

“Her body is rejecting everything.”

Zee already knew.

Human blood would not save her.

Vampire blood would not.

Healing magic failed around the Wolf venom.

Zee looked toward the battlefield.

Kael.

Alive because of him.

Ner.

Alive because of him.

Two times.

Two different outcomes.

His blood did not simply make copies.

It met the person already there.

Preserved.

Added.

Changed.

Maybe.

Tessa saw the look.

“No.”

Zee looked back.

“You know what I’m thinking?”

“Everyone knows what you’re thinking now.”

“That sounds invasive.”

“Your face is terrible at secrets.”

She coughed again.

Pain twisted her.

Zee crouched lower.

“Tessa.”

“No experiments.”

“I know.”

“Good.”

“I’m offering survival.”

Her expression shifted.

“What happened to Kael?”

“Maybe.”

“Maybe?”

“I still do not know what determines it.”

“Excellent sales pitch.”

He almost laughed.

Then her heartbeat stumbled.

No time.

Zee looked directly at her.

“If I do nothing, you die.”

Tessa closed her eyes.

“I know.”

“If I give you my blood, you may still die.”

“I know.”

“You may change.”

Silence.

She opened her eyes.

“Into what?”

“I do not know.”

The battlefield thundered behind them.

Tessa looked past Zee.

At Darkheart soldiers holding the line.

At Kael moving impossibly fast between them.

At a young Wolf guard dragging a wounded Witch to safety.

Then back to Zee.

“Will I still be me?”

Zee answered carefully.

“Kael is.”

“Ner is.”

“That is all I can promise.”

Tessa breathed once.

Then:

“Do it.”

Zee opened his wrist.

⸻

She drank.

One swallow.

Nothing.

Second.

Her Vampire nature reacted violently.

Fangs extended.

Veins darkened.

The Wolf venom inside her surged.

Zee almost pulled away.

Tessa grabbed his wrist.

“More.”

He let her.

Third swallow.

Her heartbeat slammed.

Vampire regeneration restarted.

Then something else happened.

The Wolf venom did not burn out.

It changed direction.

Not poison anymore.

Catalyst.

Tessa screamed.

Bones shifted beneath skin.

Not transformation.

Not yet.

Muscles tightened.

Her scent changed.

Zee froze.

Wolf.

Inside Vampire.

Real.

Her Vampire blood remained.

No erasure.

No replacement.

A second supernatural nature was entering beside it.

Her crushed leg snapped back into place violently.

She screamed louder.

Claws erupted from her hands.

Not Vampire nails.

Wolf claws.

Her eyes opened.

Predatory.

Wild.

Still Tessa.

Then she bit Zee’s wrist harder by instinct.

He did not pull away.

“Enough.”

She growled.

Actually growled.

Zee’s eyes narrowed.

“Enough.”

Vampire dominance hit.

Tessa froze.

Then—

resisted.

Not much.

But more than before.

Wolf aggression pushing against Vampire submission.

Interesting.

Zee tightened the command.

“Release.”

She did.

Immediately recoiled.

Horror filled her face.

“I bit you.”

“Yes.”

“I’m sorry.”

“Do not start that.”

“I lost control.”

“You were dying.”

“That is not a defense.”

Good.

Still herself.

Zee smiled faintly.

“No.”

Then the Brann artillery fired again.

The battlefield remembered them.

Zee stood.

“Tessa, stay here.”

She pushed herself upright.

Her crushed leg held.

Zee stared.

“So that is a no.”

Tessa looked equally shocked.

“I think my leg works.”

The medic whispered:

“That was pulverized.”

Tessa stood.

Vampire healing alone should not have repaired it that fast under Wolf venom.

But the venom was no longer venom.

The Wolf nature had changed everything.

Tessa looked toward the battle.

Then her nose twitched.

She froze.

“What?”

“I can smell them.”

“Who?”

“Brann.”

She turned toward the southern woods.

“Flanking.”

Zee heard nothing yet.

Vampire senses caught heartbeats seconds later.

She had scented them first.

Wolf.

Complete enough to matter immediately.

Zee smiled.

“Stay behind me.”

Tessa looked insulted.

“I am older than you.”

“I am King.”

“That has nothing to do with age.”

Fair.

They went together.

⸻

Brann’s flank expected wounded defenders.

Instead they found Zee Darkheart.

That was unfortunate.

They also found Tessa.

That was historic.

The first Wolf attacked her.

Tessa moved on Vampire instinct.

Too fast.

Caught his arm.

Then Wolf instinct changed the angle.

She twisted with the attack rather than against it.

Claws extended.

The enemy smelled her.

His face changed.

“Vampire.”

Tessa smiled.

“Yes.”

Then her own scent reached him.

The Wolf froze.

“No.”

Tessa looked briefly confused.

Then understood.

“Yes.”

She threw him through a tree.

Zee almost laughed.

No time.

Ten attackers.

He took four.

Silent Witchcraft slammed one into another.

Vampire speed put him behind the third.

Assassin knife ended the fourth.

Tessa fought two.

Not polished.

Not Kael.

Not Zee.

New.

Her Vampire strength hit first.

Wolf aggression followed.

She took a blade through the shoulder, snarled, healed, and kept moving.

One attacker fled.

Tessa’s head snapped toward him.

Pursuit instinct.

Zee saw it arrive.

The Wolf inside her wanted chase.

She wanted it too.

Then remembered the wounded behind them.

Choice.

She stayed.

Good.

Not controlled by nature.

Person.

The remaining Brann soldiers surrendered when Zee’s predatory presence rolled through the trees.

He looked at them.

“Leave Darkheart.”

They obeyed.

Not compulsion.

Fear.

Better.

⸻

The war ended before nightfall.

Brann withdrew after losing its third artillery line.

No conquest.

No annexation.

Darkheart kept its forest.

That should have been the story.

It was not.

The story became Tessa Vale.

A Vampire battlefield healer entered the battle dying.

She walked out with a Wolf’s claws.

Kael found her sitting beside a medical wagon.

He stared.

Tessa stared back.

“You too?”

Kael smiled.

“Apparently.”

Ner arrived later.

Gold.

Bloodsong.

Examination with permission.

He listened to Tessa’s blood.

Then looked at Zee.

“Vampire.”

“Yes.”

“Wolf.”

“Yes.”

“Both stable.”

There it was again.

Kael leaned against the wagon.

“So what do we call this one?”

Tessa glared.

“This one has a name.”

Kael immediately raised both hands.

“Fair.”

Zee smiled.

Good.

Person first.

Tessa looked toward her claws.

They retracted slowly.

“Vampire-Wolf.”

Ner nodded.

“Seems obvious.”

Tessa looked at Kael.

“You got Witch-Vampire?”

“Yes.”

“That is disappointingly practical.”

“We are founding history under pressure.”

“Could have tried harder.”

Zee laughed.

Actual laughter.

Short.

Rare.

Tessa looked toward him.

Then became serious.

“You knew this might happen?”

“No.”

“You hoped?”

Zee considered.

“I hoped you would live.”

“That is not the same.”

“No.”

She nodded.

Good.

⸻

By autumn, two original hybrids existed inside Darkheart.

Kael Marrin.

Witch-Vampire.

Tessa Vale.

Vampire-Wolf.

Neither belonged to Zee.

Neither served because blood demanded it.

Kael stayed in the guard.

Tessa returned to battlefield medicine and started learning her Wolf senses because apparently smelling infections before symptoms appeared was useful.

Neither became an army.

But the world did not care about nuance.

Rumors multiplied.

King Zee can combine species.

True, apparently.

King Zee can build supernatural bloodlines at will.

False.

King Zee is replacing ordinary soldiers.

False.

King Zee can create Tribrids.

Unknown and deeply alarming.

Darkheart is manufacturing monsters.

Wrong.

Then the first border kingdom closed trade.

A second recalled its ambassador.

A third sent spies.

A Vampire court offered Tessa a fortune to defect.

A Witch kingdom tried bribing Kael.

Both refused.

Their choice.

Zee approved.

Then refugees increased.

Because fear worked both directions.

If the old kingdoms feared hybrids—

people with dangerous blood knew exactly where to run.

Darkheart.

The gates widened.

New homes spread beyond Victor’s old walls.

Markets changed.

Patrols became mixed.

Witch.

Vampire.

Wolf.

Now two hybrids among them.

Zee stood on the western tower with Ner one evening.

Below, Kael argued with Tessa over whether Vampire hunger became worse when Wolf instinct wanted the same prey.

Tessa claimed yes.

Kael claimed she was dramatic.

They nearly started fighting.

Ner smiled.

“They are becoming friends.”

Zee watched.

“Terrible.”

“You like it.”

“Yes.”

Then his expression cooled.

Beyond Darkheart’s walls, another refugee caravan approached.

More people.

More responsibility.

More targets.

Ner looked toward him.

“Two.”

Zee knew what he meant.

Two hybrids.

“Yes.”

“What happens when the world sees enough of them?”

Zee watched children running beside the incoming wagons.

“They attack harder.”

“And then?”

His crimson-and-gold eyes shifted slowly into slits.

Zee looked over the kingdom the old world kept trying to frighten back into obedience.

Witches.

Vampires.

Wolves.

Outcasts.

Mixed families.

Kael.

Tessa.

People choosing him.

Then he answered.

“Then we survive harder.”

Far beyond the walls, rulers were beginning to ask how many new bloodlines King Zee Darkheart could create.

Inside Darkheart, Zee was asking a different question.

How many burials could he prevent?

And with every attack, the answer was becoming more dangerous.

Chapter Eighty

The Kingdom That Came to Darkheart

By the time Zee turned twenty-three, Darkheart had outgrown Victor’s walls.

New streets spread south.

Wolf families built along the forest line.

Vampires claimed the old underground wine tunnels and turned them into homes.

Witches expanded the outer wards instead of arguing about who belonged inside them.

Kael trained guards.

Tessa ran battlefield medicine.

Neither liked being called historic.

Both were.

The attacks kept coming.

So did the people.

One morning, five hundred refugees appeared outside Darkheart.

Not fleeing one battle.

Fleeing a kingdom.

Zee stood above the gate with Rez, Ner, and Zareth.

Zareth had arrived in human form, dark clothes edged with Drakonis markings.

He looked over the crowd.

“That is not a caravan.”

Rez nodded.

“That is a town.”

Ner’s Bloodsong brushed the people below.

Fear.

Exhaustion.

Injuries.

Children.

“No immediate threat.”

Zee looked toward the banners.

House Ardyn.

A Wolf kingdom.

Or what remained of one.

Their ruler had ordered every Witch living among the clans surrendered after discovering Darkheart’s new hybrids.

The Wolves refused.

Civil war followed.

Now an entire border province had walked away.

Their leader approached the gate.

A broad Wolf woman named Commander Sera Rhone.

She stopped before Zee.

“We want sanctuary.”

Zee looked behind her.

“You brought soldiers.”

“Seventy.”

“Families?”

“Four hundred twenty-nine.”

“Witches?”

“One hundred six.”

“Wolves?”

“The rest.”

“And your king?”

Sera smiled without humor.

“Wants our heads.”

Zee’s pupils narrowed.

“Why mine?”

“Because we heard Darkheart does not care what blood someone is born with.”

Zee looked toward Ner.

Then Kael standing below.

Then Tessa.

Darkheart’s reputation had become law before Zee ever wrote it.

He looked back at Sera.

“Enter.”

Merek nearly choked.

“Majesty, five hundred people?”

Zee glanced at him.

“Build.”

Merek stared.

Zee smiled faintly.

“You knew what job this was becoming.”

“I did not know you intended to collect entire provinces.”

“I didn’t.”

Sera overheard.

“That is disappointing.”

Rez laughed.

⸻

House Ardyn attacked six days later.

Not Darkheart Castle.

The new settlement outside it.

Smart.

The outer wards were unfinished.

Zee was in the eastern district when the first explosion hit.

By the time he reached the wall, Sera’s people were already fighting.

Good.

Darkheart did not wait for its King anymore.

Kael hit one assault line with Witchcraft and Vampire speed.

Tessa tracked infiltrators through smoke by scent.

Ner stood on the wall.

His voice carried across the battlefield.

“DOWN.”

Bloodsong hit a group of attacking Wolves.

Seven collapsed.

Not unconscious.

Bodies obeying before minds could recover.

Ner looked almost annoyed by how effective it had become.

Rez shouted from the western tower.

“Siege line moving north!”

Zareth answered through the Link before Zee could.

I see it.

Then aloud:

“I have the siege engines.”

His human body shifted.

True Dragon form erupted above the walls.

Massive wings opened.

Teal-and-Gold fire struck the empty ground in front of the siege crews.

Warning.

Most fled.

Two engines kept moving.

Zareth destroyed them.

Zee smiled.

Then smelled poison.

Behind him.

A blade entered between his ribs.

The assassin whispered:

“Monster.”

Zee looked down.

Then back.

Crimson-black scales had slowed the strike enough.

He grabbed the assassin’s wrist.

“You people desperately need new material.”

Snap.

The man screamed.

Zee bit him.

Fed.

Supernatural blood.

Wolf.

Foreign Witch poison.

His body separated both.

The poison burned.

Then failed.

Zee dropped the assassin.

Alive.

Barely.

“Who sent you?”

“Ardyn.”

“Obviously.”

Zee looked toward the attacking army.

Then the refugees behind Darkheart walls.

The answer came easily.

“Tell your king something.”

The assassin coughed.

“What?”

Zee’s crimson-and-gold eyes became slits.

“These people chose Darkheart.”

He leaned closer.

“That means he lost them.”

⸻

House Ardyn withdrew before sunset.

Not destroyed.

Defeated.

Sera stood beside Zee afterward.

“You could conquer them now.”

“Yes.”

“You won’t?”

“No.”

“Why?”

Zee looked at the wounded being carried home.

“Because I do not want their kingdom.”

Sera studied him.

“What do you want?”

Zee looked toward Darkheart.

Old Witch towers.

New Vampire districts.

Wolf settlements.

Refugee roads.

Hybrid defenders.

His answer surprised even him.

“For mine to survive.”

That night, the five hundred refugees became Darkheart citizens.

No blood oath.

No ownership.

Choice.

The borders moved again.

Not because Zee conquered land.

Because people brought their lives with them.

And the old world began realizing something worse than King Zee creating hybrids.

He was creating a place people were willing to abandon kingdoms for.

⸻

Chapter Eighty-One

The Third Beginning

The first Wolf-Witch was created four months later.

Her name was Amara Rhone.

Sera’s younger sister.

Twenty-six.

Wolf scout.

Terrible liar.

Excellent tracker.

No Witchcraft.

At least none anyone knew about.

The attack that changed her came during a night patrol beyond Darkheart’s new southern boundary.

Demon raiders struck a refugee camp.

Not for Zee.

Not for hybrids.

For people.

Bodies to sell.

Darkheart defenders stopped them.

Amara stayed behind to cover the evacuation.

By the time Zee arrived, the Demons were dead.

Amara was dying.

Again.

Too late.

Again.

Sera knelt beside her sister.

Blood covered both hands.

“What happened?”

Tessa answered.

“Demon blade through the chest.”

“Vampire blood?”

“Won’t take.”

“Witch healing?”

Kael shook his head.

“Something is consuming the magic.”

Zee crouched.

Amara opened one eye.

“You look terrible.”

Zee almost smiled.

“You have a hole in your chest.”

“Still prettier.”

Sera laughed once through tears.

Then broke.

“Zee.”

He knew.

Ner stood behind him.

Kael and Tessa too.

Proof.

Two lives already.

Two changes.

Still no certainty.

Zee looked at Amara.

“You know what happened to them.”

She glanced toward Kael.

Then Tessa.

“Yes.”

“You may change.”

“Probably.”

“You may still die.”

“Less appealing.”

Sera grabbed her hand.

“Amara—”

Amara looked at her sister.

“I want to live.”

Simple.

Zee opened his wrist.

Amara drank.

Once.

Twice.

The Demon wound reacted.

Black energy surged through her chest.

Her Wolf nature exploded outward.

Claws.

Fangs.

A growl deep enough to shake her body.

Then—

magic answered.

Not Zee’s.

Not borrowed.

Hers.

Green-white Witch light burst from Amara’s hands.

Everyone froze.

Sera stared.

“Amara?”

Amara screamed.

The Demon corruption burned away.

Wolf healing accelerated.

Witch Mana flowed into the wound beside it.

Two natures.

Not Vampire.

Wolf.

Witch.

Zee pulled his wrist away.

Amara’s heartbeat steadied.

Ner’s eyes widened.

“Zee.”

“I know.”

“No.”

Ner moved closer.

Pure Gold spread around Amara.

“There was Witch blood already inside her.”

Sera frowned.

“That’s impossible.”

Ner shook his head.

“Dormant.”

Old.

Buried somewhere in the family line.

Zee’s blood had not invented Witchcraft from nothing.

It had awakened what was already waiting.

Amara opened her eyes.

Wolf-gold.

Then Witch light flashed through them.

She looked down at her hands.

A small green flame hovered above one palm.

“Oh.”

Kael smiled.

“That seems inconvenient.”

Tessa elbowed him.

Amara stared at Zee.

“What did you do?”

Zee looked at Kael.

Witch-Vampire.

Then Tessa.

Vampire-Wolf.

Then Amara.

Wolf-Witch.

Three beginnings.

Three people.

Three lives that should have ended.

“I gave you a chance.”

Amara looked at the flame.

Then at her claws.

Sera laughed through tears.

“You are going to be unbearable.”

Amara smiled weakly.

“I already was.”

Good.

Still her.

⸻

The name came weeks later.

Wolf-Witch.

Again simple.

Again accurate.

Again chosen by the person living it.

Amara refused every dramatic alternative.

Kael suggested Moon Witch.

She threw a cup at him.

Tessa suggested Fangcaster.

Amara threatened murder.

Zee approved of neither.

Ner laughed hardest.

By winter, Darkheart had three original hybrids living inside its borders.

Kael Marrin.

Witch-Vampire.

Tessa Vale.

Vampire-Wolf.

Amara Rhone.

Wolf-Witch.

None created as soldiers.

All created because Zee refused another grave when his blood might offer life.

That distinction did not survive outside Darkheart.

Foreign reports said:

THE TRIBRID HAS COMPLETED THREE HYBRID BLOODLINES.

Another:

DARKHEART CAN NOW COMBINE THE THREE GREAT SUPERNATURAL RACES.

Another:

KING ZEE IS BUILDING AN ARMY THAT WILL REPLACE WITCHES, VAMPIRES, AND WOLVES.

False.

Terrifying.

Effective.

Then six kingdoms closed their borders to Darkheart citizens.

Two began mobilizing soldiers.

A Vampire court offered an alliance.

Three Wolf clans requested sanctuary.

A Witch House secretly asked whether Zee would save their dying heir.

And somewhere beyond the eastern mountains, an unknown kingdom issued a bounty for one thing.

Not Zee’s death.

His blood.

Zee read the notice in the throne room.

Rez stood beside him.

Ner leaned against the table.

Zareth, human for once, read over Zee’s shoulder.

“How much?” Zareth asked.

Zee looked at the number.

Then frowned.

“That is insulting.”

Rez laughed.

Ner stared at him.

“Someone wants to bleed you dry.”

“Yes.”

“And your concern is the price?”

“It should be higher.”

Zareth nodded seriously.

“I agree.”

Ner closed his eyes.

“I hate all of you.”

Zee smiled.

Then folded the bounty notice.

His eyes shifted into slits.

Three hybrids now existed because people tried to kill Darkheart.

Three new bloodlines.

Three survivors.

The world had feared what Zee might create.

So it attacked.

And the attacks created exactly what it feared.

Zee looked toward the growing kingdom beyond the windows.

“Let them come.”

Ner’s expression sharpened.

“Careful.”

Zee looked at him.

Then smiled.

Not reckless.

Not young.

Not waiting either.

“They keep teaching me what my people need.”

And that was the problem.

Every attack made Darkheart harder to kill.

Every loss made Zee more willing to change the rules.

And the Age of Hybrids had only begun.

Chapter Eighty-Two

The Price of Crimson Blood

The bounty brought hunters from five kingdoms.

Not together.

That mattered.

Some wanted money.

Some wanted Zee’s blood.

Some wanted proof the hybrids could be reproduced.

One man claimed he wanted all three.

Zee killed him first.

The hunter made the mistake of entering Darkheart disguised as a healer.

He carried glass needles under his sleeves and Dragonbane beneath his tongue.

Zee smelled both before the man reached the throne.

“Stop.”

The hunter froze.

Not completely.

Strong resistance.

Zee looked up from the petition he had been reading.

Crimson-and-gold eyes.

Human pupils.

Calm.

“Take your hands out of your sleeves.”

The man’s jaw tightened.

Vampire compulsion pushed harder.

Slowly, his hands appeared.

Needles.

The court went silent.

Zee sighed.

“That was disappointing.”

The hunter moved anyway.

Three needles flew.

Zee flicked two fingers.

All three reversed.

One hit the floor.

One buried in a pillar.

The third stopped an inch from the hunter’s eye.

Silent Witchcraft.

Zee stood.

The man backed away.

“You are worth more alive.”

Zee smiled faintly.

“There it is.”

He crossed the room before the hunter could breathe.

Vampire speed.

One hand caught the throat.

The other removed the poison capsule before the man could bite down.

Nanda Parbat.

Clean.

Automatic.

“Who hired you?”

“Bounty is public.”

“Who wrote it?”

The hunter smiled.

“Does it matter?”

Zee’s pupils narrowed.

“Yes.”

Resistance broke under the next command.

“Kingdom of Orath.”

New kingdom.

New reason.

Not fear.

Commerce.

Zee’s expression hardened.

“They put a price on my blood.”

“Yes.”

“How many hunters?”

“I don’t know.”

Truth.

Zee looked toward Merek.

“Alive.”

The hunter blinked.

Relief.

Then Zee added:

“Until we know who else bought copies.”

Relief vanished.

Better.

⸻

The next three hunters never reached Darkheart.

Kael caught one on the eastern road.

Tessa found another by scent after he poisoned a supply wagon.

Amara tracked the third for two days through mountain rain.

Zee was not present for any of it.

That mattered more than the kills.

Kael brought his hunter back alive.

Tessa did not.

“He poisoned children’s medicine,” she said.

Zee nodded.

No lecture.

Amara arrived carrying hers by the back of his coat.

“He cried.”

Kael looked over.

“You dragged him twelve miles?”

“Yes.”

“Why?”

“He was annoying.”

Tessa laughed.

Zee almost did.

Then Ner entered.

His expression killed the humor.

“What?”

Ner held a small vial.

Red.

Dark.

Zee smelled it immediately.

His own blood.

Everyone went still.

“Where?”

“From the hunter Tessa killed.”

Tessa’s face changed.

“I searched him.”

“I know.”

Ner held the vial carefully.

“It was sewn inside his boot.”

Zee took it.

One drop.

Maybe two.

Old.

Weeks old.

His blood.

Stolen before the bounty was issued.

That changed the problem.

“Someone already had access.”

Rez had arrived from Vesper that morning.

He stepped closer.

“Battlefield?”

“Possible.”

“Medical treatment?”

“Possible.”

Ner shook his head.

“Not recent.”

Zee’s face went cold.

The bounty was not only asking hunters to collect blood.

Someone had given them proof it could be collected.

A sample.

Maybe more.

Merek asked:

“What do we do?”

Zee looked toward the vial.

Once, he would have hunted the thief.

Now he thought larger.

“How much of my blood is stored in Darkheart?”

Silence.

Ner answered first.

“Medical archives.”

“Research vault.”

“Old battle samples.”

Zee looked at Merek.

“Destroy everything that is not necessary.”

Merek hesitated.

“Some records—”

“Keep records.”

Zee’s hand closed around the vial.

“Burn blood.”

Kael frowned.

“All of it?”

Zee looked at him.

“All of mine.”

Then at the hybrids.

“And yours gets secured by your choice.”

Good.

Not ownership.

Kael nodded.

Tessa did too.

Amara said:

“Burn mine.”

Ner looked at Zee.

“You are learning.”

Zee frowned.

“I hate when everyone says that.”

Rez smiled.

“Because it keeps happening.”

⸻

That night, the Crimson Archive burned.

Not the documents.

Only blood.

Old vials.

Bandages.

Battle samples.

Anything carrying Zee’s blood without immediate need.

Crimson fire consumed it.

Zee watched from the courtyard.

Ner beside him.

Zareth stood in human form near the gate.

“Someone will still try.”

Zee nodded.

“I know.”

“You cannot destroy every drop you have ever shed.”

“I know.”

Zareth looked toward him.

“Then what is the point?”

Zee’s eyes shifted to slits.

“To make stealing it expensive.”

That answer Zareth liked.

Through the Link came approval.

Then irritation.

Distance.

Drakonis.

A message arriving there.

Zareth’s face changed.

“What?”

Zee felt it before he asked.

Bounty notice.

Not on Zee.

On Zareth.

For a living Drakonis Dragon scale.

Rez stared.

“You too?”

Zareth looked offended.

“My price is higher.”

Zee turned slowly.

“How much?”

Zareth told him.

Silence.

Then Zee looked furious.

Ner stared.

“You are offended.”

“Yes.”

“Because his bounty is higher?”

“Yes.”

Rez started laughing.

Even Zareth smiled.

The moment broke the tension.

Briefly.

Then another messenger entered.

Not Darkheart.

Wolf.

From the eastern refugee settlements.

“Majesty.”

Zee turned.

The messenger was bleeding.

“Speak.”

“Three hybrid families were taken.”

The room changed.

Zee’s humor disappeared.

“Which hybrids?”

The messenger swallowed.

“None.”

Silence.

“They were ordinary mixed families.”

Witch father.

Wolf mother.

Vampire aunt.

Children with uncertain inheritance.

Taken because kidnappers believed Darkheart could turn them into something valuable.

There it was.

The fear had become market.

Not just war.

Not just kings.

Trade.

Zee’s expression went empty.

That frightened everyone more than anger.

“Where?”

The messenger pointed east.

Zee looked toward Kael, Tessa, and Amara.

Three people saved from death.

Now the world was trying to turn everyone near them into merchandise.

His philosophy shifted again.

Not just harder to kill.

Harder to take.

“Seal the eastern roads.”

Merek nodded.

“Army?”

“No.”

Zee’s pupils narrowed.

“Hunters.”

Kael smiled faintly.

Tessa cracked her knuckles.

Amara’s Wolf eyes brightened.

Not weapons.

People choosing to act.

Good.

Zee looked toward the east.

The Age of Hybrids had created something he had not expected.

A black market.

Fine.

He would teach it fear.

⸻

Chapter Eighty-Three

The Market of Living Blood

The kidnappers sold people beneath a ruined amphitheater.

Zee found the place two nights later.

Not because he was the best tracker.

Amara was.

She stood at the edge of the ravine in Wolf form, nose low.

Then shifted back.

Human.

Mud on her boots.

“They moved thirty-two captives through here.”

Kael looked toward the road.

“Thirty-two?”

Tessa’s face hardened.

“We are missing fourteen.”

Zee looked at Amara.

“Others?”

“Yes.”

“From where?”

“Everywhere.”

Not Darkheart only.

Good.

Worse.

The market had existed before Zee.

Hybrid fear had merely increased demand.

That mattered.

This was not another organization born solely because of him.

It was an old cruelty finding a new product.

Zee hated that more.

⸻

The amphitheater held sixty buyers.

Nobles.

Alchemists.

Vampires.

Witches.

One Demon.

Three Wolf lords.

Some wore masks.

Pointless.

Zee could smell bloodlines.

Kael stood beside him in the upper tunnel.

“You cannot kill everyone.”

Zee looked at him.

“I know.”

Tessa leaned against the wall.

“That sounded reluctant.”

“It was.”

Amara studied the floor below.

“Captives are underneath.”

Ner’s Bloodsong touched Zee from the far side of the structure.

He and Rez had taken the lower route.

Zareth remained outside in human form, prepared to become very large if anyone tried escaping by air.

Through the Link:

Three exits. One caravan already moving west.

Zee answered privately.

Stop it. Quietly.

Zareth’s amusement came with the thought.

You ask a Dragon to be quiet often.

Try harder.

Then the Link shifted.

Movement.

He was gone.

Zee looked toward the auction floor.

A man in red robes raised his hands.

“Tonight’s final offering.”

Chains opened below.

Four children were brought out.

The oldest maybe twelve.

The youngest six.

Zee stopped breathing.

Not because he needed air.

Because rage had become very precise.

The auctioneer smiled.

“Mixed lineage. Unconfirmed manifestation. Perfect candidates for Crimson conversion.”

Silence inside Zee.

Kael whispered:

“Oh, no.”

Not fear for Zee.

Fear for them.

The auctioneer continued.

“Imagine what Darkheart’s blood could make—”

Zee dropped from the balcony.

⸻

He landed in the center of the stage.

Stone cracked.

The entire amphitheater went silent.

The auctioneer stared.

Zee stood slowly.

Crimson-and-gold eyes.

Human pupils.

For one second.

Then slits.

“You wanted Darkheart blood.”

No one moved.

Zee smiled faintly.

“Here I am.”

Panic exploded.

Some buyers ran.

Wrong.

Some attacked.

Worse.

Some tried grabbing captives.

Worst.

Zee lifted one hand.

“Still.”

The command was not one thing.

Witchcraft struck bodies.

Vampire dominance struck minds.

Predatory presence filled the arena.

Twenty people froze.

Another fifteen resisted.

Good.

Stronger beings.

Interesting.

Kael dropped beside the captives.

Witch shield first.

Vampire speed second.

Tessa hit the lower guards.

Amara went after the cages.

Ner’s Gold erupted beneath the arena.

Every chain around the children unlocked at once.

Rez shouted from below:

“West tunnel secure!”

Zee looked at the auctioneer.

The man ran.

Zee let him.

For five seconds.

Then transformed.

Wolf.

Near-black fur.

Crimson-and-gold eyes.

He chased.

⸻

The auctioneer knew the tunnels.

Zee knew fear.

That was enough.

Left.

Down.

Across stone.

Through old water.

The man used scent powder.

Zee followed disturbed dust.

He crossed an underground stream.

Zee found blood from a blister on his heel.

He doubled back.

Zee had already circled ahead.

The auctioneer stopped.

Wolf Zee stood in the tunnel.

Huge.

Silent.

Slit pupils.

The man whispered:

“No.”

Zee shifted human.

“Who owns the market?”

The auctioneer backed away.

“No one.”

Truth.

Interesting.

“Who runs it?”

“Five brokers.”

“Names.”

“I can pay you.”

Zee smiled.

“Wrong answer.”

The man reached for a poison blade.

Zee caught the wrist.

Broke it.

“Names.”

Compulsion hit.

The auctioneer fought.

Strong charm.

Zee pressed harder.

Names came.

Five brokers.

Different cities.

Different kingdoms.

A network.

Not one mastermind.

Good.

Zee memorized them.

Then asked:

“How many children have you sold?”

The man said nothing.

Heartbeat.

Fear.

Guilt.

Enough.

“How many?”

“Hundreds.”

Something in Zee went very quiet.

The auctioneer began begging.

Zee listened.

No information left.

No reason for mercy.

He fed.

Completely.

Slow enough for the man to understand why.

Zee enjoyed the fear.

Did not apologize.

When he finished, he returned to the arena with blood on his mouth.

⸻

The fight was almost over.

That pleased him.

Kael had protected the captives without killing anyone unnecessarily.

Tessa broke three buyers and kept two alive for testimony.

Amara found seventeen more prisoners beneath the eastern tunnel.

Ner had used Bloodsong to stop a Vampire buyer from draining a child without touching the child’s circulation.

Rez had organized the escape routes so efficiently that civilians were already leaving before Zee returned.

Zareth walked in through the main entrance in human form.

His coat was torn.

Zee looked at him.

“You were supposed to be outside.”

“I was.”

“What happened?”

“Caravan.”

“And?”

“Stopped.”

Through the Link came the additional truth.

Broken wagon.

Three unconscious guards.

One terrified horse.

Zee stared.

“You frightened the horse.”

“It was dramatic.”

“You are enormous.”

“I was in human form.”

“You are still dramatic.”

Zareth smiled.

Good.

Then Ner approached.

His expression serious.

“Thirty-six captives.”

Zee’s face changed.

“All alive?”

“Thirty-four.”

There it was.

Cost.

Two dead before they arrived.

Again.

Not enough.

Never enough.

Zee looked toward the freed children.

One girl held Kael’s hand.

A Wolf boy had wrapped himself around Tessa’s waist.

Amara carried the youngest.

The sight did something dangerous.

Not soft.

Resolute.

People kept building systems around taking bodies.

So Darkheart would build systems around making that impossible.

“Rez.”

Rez looked over.

“Yes?”

“Safe roads.”

“For refugees?”

“For everyone entering Darkheart.”

Rez’s expression sharpened.

“Patrolled?”

“Yes.”

“Mixed patrols.”

“Yes.”

“Waystations.”

“Yes.”

“Blood wards.”

Ner added:

“Consent-based identification only.”

Zee nodded.

Good.

Tessa looked over.

“Rescue teams.”

Kael added:

“Permanent.”

Amara said:

“Trackers.”

Zareth folded his arms.

“Air watch.”

Zee looked around.

There.

Not Zee saving everyone.

Structure.

Kingdom.

People.

A system built because the world kept forcing one.

“Do it.”

No ceremony.

No decree speech.

Just decision.

⸻

The first Darkheart Safe Road opened before autumn ended.

Then three more.

Patrolled by Witches.

Vampires.

Wolves.

Kael trained mixed-response units.

Tessa built emergency medical stations.

Amara organized trackers.

Ner developed blood-resonance alarms that could identify distress without reading private thoughts.

Rez helped design supply routes.

Zareth added Drakonis air signals over shared borders.

Darkheart got harder to raid.

Harder to kidnap from.

Harder to isolate.

The market responded.

Prices on Darkheart citizens doubled.

Then tripled.

Fear and greed feeding each other.

Zee read the new notices in his throne room.

One buyer had posted a reward for a living Witch-Vampire.

Kael.

Another for a Vampire-Wolf.

Tessa.

A third for a Wolf-Witch.

Amara.

Zee’s eyes turned to slits.

Merek waited.

“What do you want done?”

Zee looked at the names of the five brokers.

Then at the bounties.

Once, he waited for attacks.

Then he stopped plans.

Now people were openly purchasing the lives of his citizens.

That was enough.

“Find the brokers.”

Merek nodded.

“Capture?”

Zee considered.

“Bring me proof first.”

“And after?”

Zee’s expression remained calm.

That was the frightening part.

“If they are still selling people…”

His fangs descended slightly.

“…there will be fewer brokers.”

Outside, another refugee caravan approached Darkheart under escort from the new Safe Road patrol.

Inside, the kingdom kept changing.

Not into an army.

Into something harder.

A place with teeth.

And every time the old world invented a new way to prey on Zee’s people, King Zee Darkheart answered by making the kingdom itself more difficult to hunt.
