Chapter One Hundred Twelve

The Prince Darkheart Was Allowed to Know

Darkheart learned about Zayrlen because Ner got tired of hiding him.

By the sixth month, hiding the pregnancy required more effort than either man considered reasonable.

Ner stood before the mirror one morning fastening a coat that no longer closed correctly.

He pulled once.

Nothing.

Again.

Still nothing.

Zee watched from the bed.

“Stop.”

Ner looked at him through the mirror.

“Do not start.”

“You are fighting clothing.”

“It started first.”

“You own other coats.”

“I like this one.”

Zee stood.

Crimson Phoenix wings shifted behind him before folding tightly enough to cross the room.

He reached toward the fastening.

Ner slapped his hand away.

“I can dress myself.”

“I was going to help.”

“You were going to listen.”

Zee paused.

Ner stared.

Zee listened anyway.

Two heartbeats.

Steady.

Ner’s eyes narrowed.

“You are terrible at pretending.”

“Yes.”

Zayrlen moved.

The Pure Gold Mana beneath Ner’s skin responded immediately.

A thin Crimson line followed.

Then heat.

Dragon.

Witch.

Wolf.

The pattern had become unmistakable.

Zee touched Ner carefully.

Zayrlen kicked directly beneath his hand.

Zee froze.

Ner smiled.

“He did that yesterday.”

“You did not tell me.”

“You were murdering people in a flying bone ship.”

“That is not an excuse.”

“It is literally an excuse.”

Zayrlen moved again.

Harder.

Zee’s entire expression changed.

Ner watched him.

Then his smile softened.

“You want everyone to know.”

Zee looked up.

“That is your decision too.”

“I know.”

Silence.

This child was different from the son Zee had hidden.

No veil.

No erased bloodline.

No false home.

Zayrlen could be named.

Recognized.

Loved in daylight.

Ner rested a hand over their son.

“I am tired of pretending I ate too much.”

Zee almost laughed.

Ner looked at him.

“We tell Darkheart.”

“Today?”

“Yes.”

“No giant ceremony.”

“Agreed.”

“No prophecy nonsense.”

“Obviously.”

“No one touches my stomach without asking.”

Zee nodded.

“Especially Zareth.”

“Why especially Zareth?”

“He looks curious.”

Zee considered.

“He does.”

“See?”

⸻

Darkheart received the news in the central courtyard.

No throne.

No royal announcement scroll.

Ner simply walked beside Zee onto the upper steps without the coat that had hidden his pregnancy.

The courtyard quieted gradually.

Then completely.

Kael already knew.

Tessa knew.

Amara knew.

Zareth stood nearby in human form.

Rez had arrived from Vesper that morning.

The rest of Darkheart did not.

Merek looked from Ner to Zee.

Then back.

His eyes widened.

“Oh.”

Ner folded his arms.

“That reaction is why we waited.”

Someone farther back whispered:

“Is he—”

“Yes,” Zee said.

Silence again.

Ner looked at him.

“I could have answered.”

“I know.”

“Then why did you?”

“They were taking too long.”

Ner sighed.

Zee addressed the courtyard.

“Ner and I are having a son.”

The reaction hit like thunder.

Not fear.

Joy.

Wolves howled.

Witches released sparks into the air.

Vampires shouted.

Someone started crying.

Zee immediately regretted telling anyone.

Ner did not.

He stood watching Darkheart celebrate a child they had never demanded.

Nobody shouted heir.

Nobody shouted succession.

One woman shouted:

“WHAT IS HIS NAME?”

Ner smiled.

“Zayrlen Keal Darkheart.”

That made it worse.

The courtyard erupted again.

Rez leaned toward Zee.

“You look horrified.”

“There are too many people.”

“This is your kingdom.”

“That remains an unfortunate design flaw.”

Zareth looked toward Ner’s stomach.

“Can I—”

“No,” Ner said.

Zareth frowned.

“I did not finish.”

“You were going to ask to touch him.”

“Yes.”

“No.”

Through the Link came:

This is discrimination against Dragons.

Zee ignored him.

⸻

The celebration lasted until evening.

Ner escaped after twenty minutes.

Zee lasted twelve.

The important part came later.

Darkheart children began leaving small things outside Zee and Ner’s rooms.

Wooden wolves.

Carved dragons.

Gold-painted stones.

One badly made crown.

Ner picked that one up.

“He cannot wear this.”

Zee looked at it.

“It might fit Rez.”

Rez threw something at him.

For once, Zee did not mind the noise.

His son had been named publicly.

Nothing came to kill him.

No sky split.

No kingdom issued a death decree.

No father looked at the child and thought he should not exist.

Zee stood in the hall surrounded by gifts meant for Zayrlen.

For one quiet second—

the difference hurt.

Then he let it.

Aidan had received protection through secrecy.

Zayrlen was receiving protection through belonging.

Neither had been loved less.

The world had simply allowed Zee different choices.

⸻

Three days later, someone tried to steal Zayrlen’s blood.

They never reached Ner.

That was the only reason Darkheart still had an eastern medical tower.

The attacker entered disguised as one of Tessa’s assistants.

Human heartbeat.

Human scent.

No visible magic.

But Zee’s Blood Mark had taught his Vampire nature to remember signatures.

This person carried traces of blood from the bone vessels.

Zee smelled it when they crossed the council corridor.

He stopped.

The false healer stopped too.

Ner kept walking for two steps.

Then looked back.

“What?”

Zee’s eyes narrowed.

“Do I know you?”

The healer swallowed.

“No, Majesty.”

Blood pressure changed.

Heart accelerated.

Zee’s Wolf instincts caught fear.

Witch sight caught the concealment woven into the skin.

One motion.

“Sever.”

The disguise fell.

A woman stood beneath it.

Shaved head.

Gray ritual scars.

A needle appeared in her hand.

She lunged toward Ner.

She never crossed half the distance.

Zee’s Phoenix wing slammed between them.

The needle struck a feather.

Crimson fire consumed the metal.

Ner lifted one hand.

Pure Gold Mana crushed the attacker against the wall.

Hard.

She coughed.

Ner looked at Zee.

“I had that.”

“I know.”

“Then why did you move?”

“She was closer to me.”

Ner stared.

“That is a terrible lie.”

“Yes.”

The woman tried biting through her own tongue.

Heart Command hit first.

“Stop.”

Her jaw froze.

Zee approached.

“What did you want?”

She resisted.

Ner felt the heartbeat through Bloodsong.

“She is terrified of answering.”

Zee crouched.

“Good.”

The woman’s eyes flicked toward Ner.

Then his pregnancy.

Zee noticed.

His expression disappeared.

“What did you want from my son?”

Nothing.

Zee’s voice carried heavier Vampire authority.

“Speak.”

Her resistance cracked.

“Blood.”

Ner’s Gold tightened around her.

“Why?”

“Creation.”

Zee went still.

She continued because the command held.

“The unborn blood of a naturally forming multi-blood child may stabilize artificial combinations.”

Ner stopped breathing for one second.

Zee’s face became empty.

The woman realized what she had admitted.

Too late.

“Who sent you?”

“The Order of the Hollow Crown.”

A name.

Independent.

Not Pyrathis.

Not the bone-vessel force itself.

Researchers who had purchased information from the wreckage network after rumors of Zee’s creation blood spread.

Zee did not care about their ideology.

They had come for his unborn son.

That simplified everything.

“Where?”

She gave him the location.

A monastery beneath the Glass Mountains.

Ner released her from the wall.

The woman collapsed.

She looked toward Zee.

“I told you.”

“Yes.”

“You can use me.”

“No.”

“I can show you the laboratories.”

“You already gave me the location.”

She stared.

“I surrendered.”

Zee’s pupils became slits.

“You came for my son.”

The woman died before she could answer.

⸻

Ner stood over the body.

No moral lecture.

No surprise.

Just anger.

“They knew.”

“Enough.”

“They know I am carrying something unusual.”

“Yes.”

“Then the announcement—”

“Did not cause this.”

Ner looked at him.

“You are certain?”

“They had the plan before Darkheart knew.”

Good.

Zee would not let fear rewrite Zayrlen’s life before birth.

He looked toward the eastern mountains.

Ner knew that expression.

“You are going.”

“Yes.”

“I am coming.”

“No.”

Ner stared.

Zee immediately corrected:

“They targeted you and Zayrlen specifically.”

“That is exactly why I am coming.”

“You are six months pregnant.”

“I remain aware.”

“Ner.”

“Zee.”

Silence.

Then Zayrlen moved.

Both felt it.

Ner put a hand over his stomach.

“Your son apparently has an opinion.”

Zee listened.

The heartbeat was fast.

Not distressed.

Wolf response.

The child had reacted to both fathers’ agitation.

Crimson and Gold shimmered beneath Ner’s hand.

Zee exhaled.

“You stay with the second line.”

Ner smiled.

“Negotiable.”

“Ner.”

“Fine.”

It was not fine.

Both knew that.

⸻

Chapter One Hundred Thirteen

The Blood That Would Not Stay Broken

The Glass Mountains reflected sunlight like knives.

The Order of the Hollow Crown had built beneath them because the crystalline stone disrupted ordinary magical tracking.

It did not disrupt Zee.

Not anymore.

The King’s Hunt read movement.

Blood Mark recognized the signature carried by the dead infiltrator.

Witch sight found artificial seams in the mountain.

Wolf instinct smelled people living where no settlement should exist.

Phoenix wings carried Zee over the last ridge.

Behind him came Darkheart forces.

Kael.

Amara.

Rhyven.

Ner remained with the second line exactly as promised.

For eleven minutes.

Then he walked forward.

Zee landed beside him.

“You said second line.”

“This is the second line.”

“It moved.”

“So did I.”

Zee stared.

Ner smiled.

Pregnant.

Dangerous.

Impossible.

Zee loved him.

“Stay behind me.”

“No.”

“Ner.”

“I will stay beside you.”

Zee considered arguing.

Then the mountain opened.

The Order attacked.

Argument over.

⸻

Glass soldiers emerged from concealed gates.

Not actual glass.

Witches wearing mirrored armor designed to reflect magical targeting.

Behind them came experimental creatures.

Not stitched corpses this time.

Living failures.

A Vampire with Demon bone growing through his spine.

A Witch whose arms had become blackened claws.

A Wolf with two hearts beating out of rhythm.

The Hollow Crown had learned from the bone vessels.

Not how to create.

How to break more carefully.

Rhyven saw the Wolf.

His expression changed.

“Alive?”

Zee listened.

“Yes.”

The creature charged.

Rhyven met it.

Not to kill.

To stop.

Wolf form struck Wolf form.

Rhyven’s Phoenix vitality absorbed the impact.

The altered Wolf snapped at his throat.

Rhyven rolled beneath it.

Crimson fire moved through his claws.

He deliberately kept the flames away from flesh.

Amara joined him.

Two Wolves pinning one.

Prisoner.

Not enemy.

Zee moved past them.

Good.

His people had learned his distinctions too.

⸻

The Order’s Witches raised mirrored barriers.

Zee did not slow.

Vampire speed.

Witch sight.

One structural weakness.

“Sever.”

The first barrier failed.

The second reflected the command.

Interesting.

The returning magic struck Zee.

His own severing force cut across his shoulder.

Blood opened.

Phoenix flame sealed part of it.

The Order’s Magister smiled from behind the third barrier.

“We studied you.”

Zee looked at the wound.

Then smiled.

“Not enough.”

He flew.

Straight upward.

The barrier had been designed for frontal Witch assault.

Not a winged predator entering from the ceiling.

Zee came through crystal.

Crimson Phoenix wings shielded his face.

Dragon durability took the impact.

Wolf instinct found the Magister before dust cleared.

Vampire speed closed distance.

One synchronized movement.

The Magister barely raised his hand.

Zee broke it.

“Where are the prisoners?”

Silence.

Heart Command pressed.

“Answer.”

“Below.”

“How many?”

“Forty-eight.”

“Children?”

The man’s heart changed.

Zee heard the lie forming.

“Answer correctly.”

“Six.”

Zee’s expression disappeared.

The Magister started begging before Zee touched him again.

Smart.

Useless.

⸻

Ner reached the lower chambers first.

Not because Zee allowed it.

Because Bloodsong found forty-eight terrified rhythms beneath the mountain and Ner followed them.

His Pure Gold Mana opened the first door.

Inside were cages.

He went very still.

Zayrlen’s heartbeat changed.

Fast.

Wolf agitation.

Ner placed one hand over his stomach.

“I know.”

The nearest prisoner looked up.

A young Witch man.

Black veins covered half his face.

One eye burned red.

The other remained blue.

His hands shook uncontrollably.

Ner approached.

The prisoner recoiled.

“Do not touch me.”

“I was not going to.”

“They put Demon marrow in me.”

Ner’s expression hardened.

“How long?”

“Twenty days.”

“Your Witchcraft?”

“Still there.”

“What is failing?”

The man laughed weakly.

“Everything.”

His heartbeat stumbled.

Ner immediately called through Bloodsong.

Not words.

A signal Zee recognized from floors above.

Urgent.

Zee arrived seconds later.

He looked at the prisoner.

Then smelled it.

Witch.

Demon.

Neither stable.

The Order had tried combining them through marrow transplantation.

It had failed.

The Demon source was consuming the Witch structure.

The Witch Mana was burning the Demon tissue.

The body sat between them.

Dying.

Tessa was still several chambers away.

Zee crouched.

“Name.”

The prisoner blinked.

“What?”

“Your name.”

“Elias.”

Zee’s expression changed for half a second.

Then settled.

Not prophecy.

Not future connection.

Just a name.

“Elias what?”

“Elias Marr.”

“Do you want to live?”

The Witch stared.

“Yes.”

“Do you understand living may mean changing?”

A pause.

“Yes.”

“Do you understand I cannot promise what shape?”

Fear.

Then resolve.

“Yes.”

Zee looked at Ner.

Ner already understood.

“Two bloodlines.”

“Witch and Demon.”

“Their version is killing him.”

“Yes.”

Ner looked at Elias.

Then back at Zee.

“Can yours make them stop fighting?”

Zee looked deeper.

His blood answered.

Demon source.

Not a birth nature inside him.

A stable pattern integrated into his Crimson Demonic Dragon evolution.

Enough to create from.

Witch.

One of his original natures.

He could feel the bridge.

This did not need three.

It needed two done correctly.

Zee cut his palm.

“Drink.”

Elias hesitated.

Then obeyed.

⸻

The change was uglier than Rhyven’s.

No fire rebirth.

No Dragon core.

Demon biology fought through the bones.

Elias screamed.

His Witch Mana exploded around the cage.

Ner raised Pure Gold barriers around the nearby prisoners.

Zee held Elias down.

The man’s blackened veins spread.

Then stopped.

Crimson blood reached them.

Did not erase Demon.

Did not erase Witch.

Rewrote the conflict.

Witch Mana began forming channels around the Demon structure instead of attacking it.

Demon marrow stopped consuming the magic and became an anchor for it.

Elias’s hands transformed.

Black claws appeared.

Then receded when he panicked.

His eyes changed.

Both became blue again.

Then thin black rings formed around the irises.

His Witch Mana returned.

Not Gold.

Not Crimson.

His original deep blue.

But now black demonic sigils lived inside it.

One stable expression.

Elias screamed once more.

Then the two rhythms became one.

Witch.

Demon.

Stable.

A new race.

Zee listened.

Alive.

Strong.

Still Elias.

He released him.

Elias lay shaking.

“What am I?”

Zee looked at the blue Witch light curling around black claws.

“Demon–Witch.”

Ner stared.

“Another first.”

“Yes.”

Elias looked terrified.

Zee crouched.

“You are not theirs.”

The Witch looked at him.

“They made this.”

“No.”

Zee’s eyes hardened.

“They broke you.”

Then he offered his hand.

“I made sure you survived it.”

Elias took it.

⸻

The Hollow Crown realized its lower prison had been breached.

Every experiment was ordered terminated.

That killed any possibility of mercy.

Glass vents opened.

Black gas flooded the cages.

Ner smelled it first.

“Poison.”

Zee’s wings opened.

“Hold your breath.”

Ner looked offended.

“I am Vampire.”

“Still.”

Zee slammed both Phoenix wings outward.

Crimson fire entered the ventilation channels.

Not into the prisoners.

Into the poison.

The gas ignited.

Burned away before reaching the cages.

Above them, bells sounded.

Execution protocol.

Zee looked toward the ceiling.

His expression became calm.

Rhyven arrived carrying an unconscious Wolf over one shoulder.

Amara behind him with two children.

Kael kicked open another cage.

“They are killing their own prisoners.”

Zee’s eyes became slits.

“Get everyone out.”

Kael looked at him.

“And you?”

Zee’s altered horns glowed faintly.

“Closing another institution.”

No one asked what that meant.

⸻

The Order of the Hollow Crown died in its own monastery.

Not every person inside.

Prisoners lived.

Servants who had not participated were removed.

Two young initiates who dropped their weapons and had never touched a captive were restrained instead of killed.

Distinctions remained.

But the researchers?

Dead.

The guards who mutilated prisoners?

Dead.

The Witches who designed forced bloodline grafts?

Dead.

The officers who ordered termination?

Dead.

The Magister who funded the child experiments?

Zee found him beneath the central dome.

The man had surrounded himself with twelve mirrored barriers.

Zee landed before them.

The Magister smiled nervously.

“You cannot break all twelve before the mountain collapses.”

Zee looked upward.

Cracks already spreading.

Then toward the prisoners evacuating through Ner’s Gold corridors.

“You are right.”

The Magister relaxed.

Zee raised one hand.

“Silence.”

Every spoken activation inside the barriers died.

Then another hand.

“Sever.”

Not all twelve.

One connection.

The shared anchor.

All twelve barriers failed together.

The Magister stared.

Zee stepped through.

“You learned from me.”

“Yes.”

Zee grabbed him.

“You should have learned the important part.”

“What?”

“Hurt my people.”

Crimson Phoenix flame spread across Zee’s hand.

“You die.”

The Magister burned.

Zee did not look away.

⸻

The mountain began collapsing.

Ner was still inside.

Zee felt his heartbeat.

Then Zayrlen’s.

Both moving.

Too slow.

“Ner.”

Bloodsong answered through the stone.

Working on it.

Zee launched downward.

Phoenix wings folded tightly through the corridor.

He found Ner beneath a broken arch, Pure Gold Mana holding twenty prisoners beneath a shield.

Zayrlen’s heartbeat hammered.

Not distress.

Reaction.

The unborn Wolf felt danger.

Crimson and Gold light spread across Ner’s abdomen.

Then something impossible happened.

A Dragon pulse rolled outward.

Heat.

Not Phoenix.

Dragon.

The broken arch above Ner cracked again.

Before Zee reached him, Pure Gold Witch Mana surged from Ner.

For one second, another magical rhythm moved beneath it.

Not Ner’s.

Zayrlen’s.

Crimson-gold.

The collapsing stone shifted sideways.

Barely.

An instinctive unborn magical reaction.

No conscious casting.

No awakened nature.

Just developing power responding to danger.

Zee landed.

His face changed.

Ner looked down at himself.

“Did he just—”

“Yes.”

“Is that bad?”

“No.”

Zee grabbed the stone.

Dragon strength lifted.

“Later.”

Together they cleared the corridor.

Ner maintained Gold around the prisoners.

Zee used Phoenix wings as a shield against falling glass.

Rhyven carried the injured.

Elias Marr walked under his own power.

Blue-black Witch Mana held one side of the tunnel.

New blood.

Old family.

Unborn life.

All moving together.

They escaped seconds before the monastery collapsed.

⸻

Darkheart brought forty-eight prisoners home.

Six children.

All alive.

Three were too damaged for transformation and remained under Tessa’s care.

Two asked Zee to change them.

He refused.

They did not need it to survive.

That answer spread too.

Zee was capable of creating races.

That did not mean he would give anyone whatever bloodline they wanted.

Rhyven understood.

Elias understood faster.

He spent the first week terrified of sleeping.

Demon instincts came with dreams.

Witch Mana answered emotion more sharply.

But neither side tried to destroy the other anymore.

His deep-blue magic now carried black sigils naturally.

When he cast, his claws sometimes appeared.

When anger rose, Demon strength entered his body.

When Witch precision returned, the Demon response followed structure instead of chaos.

One race.

Demon–Witch.

New.

Stable.

Alive.

⸻

The world learned about him within weeks.

It learned the wrong lesson again.

Rulers began listing what Zee could now create.

Phoenix.

Dragon.

Demon.

Witch.

Vampire.

Wolf.

Simple combinations.

Tribrids.

Unknown future variants.

The lists grew.

Zee ignored them.

He cared about something else.

Ner entered the seventh month.

Zayrlen’s heartbeat had become loud enough that Zee sometimes heard it from across a room.

On the next full moon, it changed again.

Ner woke before Zee.

Crimson and Gold light filled the bedroom.

Not bright.

Soft.

Alive.

Zee opened his eyes.

Ner sat upright with one hand over his stomach.

“What is he doing?”

Zee listened.

Wolf rhythm.

Witch structure.

Dragon heat.

All three.

Natural.

Synchronized before birth only as developing instinct, not active power.

Zee moved closer.

Then stopped.

Ner looked at him.

“What?”

Zee’s Phoenix wings had opened.

Completely.

Curved around the bed.

A shield.

Ner stared.

Then slowly smiled.

“You did it again.”

Zee looked at the wings.

“So?”

“You are shielding us from nothing.”

Zee listened beyond the walls.

No threat.

No assassin.

No spell.

Nothing.

He slowly folded one wing.

Ner caught the other.

“Leave it.”

Zee looked at him.

Ner leaned against the crimson feathers.

Warm.

Not burning him.

Zayrlen’s heartbeat settled beneath them.

For a few minutes, the Age of New Blood did not matter.

The kingdoms experimenting in secret did not matter.

The next race did not matter.

The next war did not matter.

There was only Zee.

Ner.

And the son growing between Crimson and Gold.

Then the eastern alarm bell rang.

Zee closed his eyes.

Ner sighed.

“The world has terrible timing.”

“Yes.”

Zee stood.

Phoenix wings opened.

Ner stood too.

Seven months pregnant.

Pure Gold Mana already gathering around one hand.

Zee looked at him.

Ner raised an eyebrow.

“Do not.”

Zee almost smiled.

Then they went to see who had made the next mistake.

Chapter One Hundred Fourteen

The Friend They Took

The eastern alarm was not an invasion.

That made it worse.

Zee reached the outer wall first.

Crimson Phoenix wings spread behind him.

Ner arrived seconds later with Pure Gold Mana around one hand and seven months of pregnancy doing absolutely nothing to improve his willingness to follow instructions.

Kael came from the southern barracks.

Amara from the training fields.

Rhyven reached the wall in a blur of Wolf speed and lingering Crimson heat.

Then Elias Marr walked out of the medical wing.

Zee turned immediately.

“You should be resting.”

Elias looked at him.

“You have been saying that to me since we were children.”

There it was.

Not prisoner.

Not stranger.

Elias.

Family.

Long before the Hollow Crown had carved Demon marrow into him, Elias Marr had been sitting at Darkheart tables.

Long before Zee became King, Elias had been one of the Witches who slipped Ner stolen kitchen wine during royal dinners.

He had trained beside Kael.

Lost money to Rez.

Argued theology with Zareth until the Dragon threatened to eat his books.

Aurelia had known him by name.

He had attended her funeral.

He had stood beside Zee when Victor’s throne finally emptied.

And six weeks before the Glass Mountains—

Elias had disappeared while escorting three Darkheart families through the northern roads.

They had found the families.

Alive.

They had not found Elias.

Until the Hollow Crown.

Whatever the Order had done to him had changed his scent, his blood, his Mana, and almost everything supernatural Zee would normally have recognized at a distance.

But Elias Marr had never been new to Darkheart.

They had simply gotten him back in pieces.

Zee looked at the fading black veins beneath Elias’s throat.

“You almost died three days ago.”

“Four.”

“That does not improve it.”

“No.”

Elias stepped beside him.

“But if the alarm is about me, I would prefer to hear why.”

Zee’s eyes narrowed.

“Why would it be about you?”

A guard approached.

Then handed him a blackened piece of bone.

It was still warm.

Elias saw it.

His expression changed.

“I know that mark.”

⸻

The bone had been driven into Darkheart soil like a message post.

Three symbols were carved across it.

None were Witch.

Rhyven smelled it and immediately backed away.

“Demon.”

Elias nodded.

“Old Demon.”

Zee looked toward him.

“How old?”

“Older than the kind the Hollow Crown was using in their cages.”

Ner touched the edge with Gold.

The bone reacted.

Black flame snapped toward his hand.

Zee caught Ner’s wrist and pulled him back.

Ner stared.

“I was fine.”

“Yes.”

“You do understand I can still use magic.”

“Yes.”

“You are doing the thing.”

“What thing?”

“Pregnancy insanity.”

Zee looked at the bone.

“That was hostile.”

“It was a spark.”

“It touched you.”

“It nearly touched me.”

“Exactly.”

Elias looked between them.

“I missed this.”

Ner turned.

“You were imprisoned for six weeks.”

“Yes.”

“And this is what you missed?”

“No. I also missed food.”

Fair.

Zee looked at the symbols.

“Translate.”

Elias’s humor disappeared.

He crouched.

Deep-blue Witch Mana gathered around his fingertips.

Black demonic sigils appeared inside it.

The symbols reacted.

His new nature recognized them.

Not because the Demon source owned him.

Because it was part of him now.

Elias read slowly.

“Return stolen marrow.”

Zee went still.

Elias continued.

“Return the vessel carrying it.”

Silence.

Rhyven looked toward him.

“You.”

“Yes.”

The final line blackened beneath Elias’s fingers.

He read it.

“Or the settlement burns until nothing bearing Darkheart blood remains.”

Zee smiled.

No humor.

“That was stupid.”

⸻

The marrow inside Elias had not come from a random Demon corpse.

The Hollow Crown had stolen it from something powerful enough that its bloodline could still feel the loss.

The source did not care that Elias had been tortured.

It did not care that the Order was dead.

It cared that part of its blood now existed beyond its ownership.

Elias stood beside Zee in the council chamber while maps were unrolled.

“You are not giving me back.”

Zee looked at him.

“That was never an option.”

“I know.”

“Then why say it?”

“Because you looked like you were planning to kill an entire region.”

“Only if necessary.”

Elias stared.

Ner sat nearby with both feet on another chair.

“He means that.”

“I know.”

Zee looked at Elias.

“How much do you remember about the marrow?”

“Pain.”

“Useful.”

“Very.”

Elias ignored him.

“The Order called it Sovereign Demon marrow.”

Zee’s expression sharpened.

“Not related to my Sovereign state.”

“No.”

“Good.”

“Different use of the word.”

Elias pointed toward the mountains east of Darkheart.

“They said the source came from a Demon ruler beneath the Iron Chasm.”

Amara frowned.

“A kingdom?”

Elias shook his head.

“A dominion.”

Zareth entered through the balcony because doors remained beneath him in spirit even when he was Human.

Teal-and-Gold Mana flickered around his hands.

Phoenix vitality had already erased the last visible Dragonbane damage.

“What did I miss?”

Rez entered from the opposite door.

“Apparently Elias is being repossessed.”

Elias looked at him.

Rez stopped.

For the first time since Elias returned, neither man joked.

Rez crossed the room.

Then punched him in the chest.

Not hard.

Elias winced anyway.

“What was that for?”

“You vanished.”

“I was captured.”

“You could have avoided that.”

“Excellent advice.”

Rez grabbed him.

The hug lasted only a few seconds.

Long enough.

When he released him, Rez looked at the black ring around Elias’s eyes.

“You look terrible.”

“You became Vampire while I was gone.”

“Yes.”

“You look worse.”

“Good. You are definitely still Elias.”

Zee watched them.

This was why the Hollow Crown had died.

Not because it experimented on some stranger.

Because it had taken someone who belonged at this table.

Someone who had belonged there for years.

The Demon–Witch first had not been given to a random man the world would forget.

It had happened to Elias Marr.

Chosen family.

And whoever wanted him now had made the mistake of assuming Zee would negotiate over one of his own.

⸻

The attack began at dusk.

No army appeared.

The shadows changed.

Darkheart’s eastern forest turned black beneath a sky that was still red with sunset.

Every animal fled west.

Wolves on the wall growled.

Vampires smelled sulfur.

Witches felt something push against the lower foundations of their magic.

Then the trees opened.

Demons walked through.

Not mutated Humans.

Not experimental things.

True Demons.

Tall.

Armored.

Some with horns.

Some with bone plates.

Some almost Human until they smiled.

At their center walked a man in black iron.

His horns curved backward.

His eyes were completely red.

He looked directly at Elias.

“There.”

Elias stepped onto the wall.

Zee’s wing blocked half his body automatically.

Elias looked at it.

“Seriously?”

“Yes.”

The Demon ruler ignored the exchange.

“My marrow.”

Elias’s claws emerged.

Black.

His deep-blue Witch Mana circled them.

“My body.”

The Demon smiled.

“No.”

Zee’s pupils narrowed.

That single word almost ended diplomacy before it began.

The Demon looked toward him.

“Zee Darkheart.”

“You know me.”

“Everyone does now.”

His gaze moved to the Crimson Phoenix wings.

“King who drinks races.”

Zee smiled.

“Only rude ones.”

Ner muttered:

“That was almost funny.”

Zee ignored him.

The Demon ruler pointed toward Elias.

“The flesh is irrelevant. The marrow belongs to House Varkesh.”

Elias’s expression hardened.

Zee’s voice went flat.

“He said no.”

“You cannot deny blood its master.”

“Yes, I can.”

“How?”

Zee opened his wings.

“Violently.”

The Demon army moved.

So did Darkheart.

⸻

Elias fought beside Zee.

Not behind him.

The first Demon struck with a bone sword.

Elias caught the wrist.

His Witch Mana formed a deep-blue binding around the arm.

Black demonic sigils grew through the spell.

The binding did not collapse under Demon strength.

It tightened.

Elias looked surprised for half a second.

Then smiled.

“Oh.”

He twisted.

The Demon’s arm broke.

Black claws entered its chest.

Elias froze.

Instinct told him to rip the heart out.

Witch precision told him exactly where.

Both answered together.

He killed the Demon.

Then stared at his hand.

Zee landed beside him.

“Problem?”

“No.”

Elias’s breathing changed.

“I liked that more than I expected.”

Zee looked at the corpse.

“Welcome home.”

No judgment.

Elias had been part of Darkheart long enough to know that answer was genuine.

Another Demon came.

Elias raised one hand.

“Hold.”

Deep-blue Witchcraft erupted.

Black sigils hardened through it like a skeletal frame.

The Demon stopped mid-lunge.

Elias’s eyes widened.

His new biology was finding itself through combat.

Witch structure.

Demon force.

Not alternating.

One race.

Demon–Witch.

He closed his hand.

The spell crushed the attacker’s armor into its ribs.

Elias smiled.

This time he did not apologize for it.

⸻

Rhyven tore through the left flank in true Wolf form.

Crimson fire ran through his claws.

Kael used Witchcraft and Vampire speed to break the center.

Amara’s Wolf patrols hunted anyone trying to reach civilians.

Zareth shifted.

True Dragon form erupted above the eastern wall.

Teal-and-Gold scales.

Original Dragon wings.

Phoenix fire tracing their edges.

Witch sigils spinning between his horns.

His Dragonfire struck the forest beyond the walls.

Not randomly.

Precisely.

A Witch-shaped structure contained the blast and prevented it from spreading toward Darkheart homes.

Zareth felt the control.

Then sent through the Link:

I am becoming annoyingly good at this.

Zee answered:

You are welcome.

I regret surviving.

Zee almost smiled.

Then the Demon ruler hit him.

⸻

The impact threw Zee through the outer watchtower.

Stone collapsed.

His wings folded around his body before the debris landed.

Phoenix feathers took the first impact.

Dragon durability took the second.

Vampire healing repaired what remained.

Wolf instinct had already tracked the Demon ruler before Zee stood.

Witch sight found the magic beneath the black armor.

Everything moved together.

Perfect.

Mastered.

Zee stepped from the ruins.

Crimson fire ran across his wings.

The Demon ruler stared.

“You contain too much.”

Zee tilted his head.

“I keep hearing that.”

The Demon attacked.

Black force split the ground.

Zee flew above it.

One wing struck.

The Demon caught it.

Bad choice.

Crimson Phoenix flame traveled into his gauntlet.

The armor began burning.

He released Zee.

Zee landed.

“Silence.”

The Demon’s next spoken invocation failed.

His eyes widened.

Zee’s Vampire speed crossed the distance.

Wolf instinct read the counterattack.

Dragon strength broke the man’s breastplate.

Witchcraft severed the defensive enchantment beneath it.

Then Zee stopped.

Not because he had to.

Because Elias stood behind the Demon.

The ruler looked toward him.

Elias’s claws were out.

Deep-blue Mana covered in black sigils surrounded both hands.

The ruler laughed.

“You think his stolen marrow makes him my equal?”

Elias looked at Zee.

No words.

Zee understood.

This death belonged to him if he wanted it.

Zee stepped back.

The Demon ruler’s smile vanished.

“You allow the vessel to decide?”

Zee’s expression became cold.

“He was deciding before you arrived.”

Elias attacked.

⸻

The Demon ruler was stronger.

Much stronger.

Elias knew it immediately.

His first strike was blocked.

The second nearly broke his spine.

The third opened his chest.

Blood hit the ground.

Zee did not interfere.

Not yet.

Elias had chosen the fight.

Family did not mean denying him the right to finish it.

The Demon grabbed Elias by the throat.

“You carry a fragment.”

Elias’s hands tightened around the arm.

“No.”

His Witch Mana flared.

“I carry me.”

A deep-blue circle formed beneath both of them.

Black demonic sigils appeared inside the lines.

The ruler looked down.

Too late.

Elias smiled.

“Fall.”

The circle inverted.

Not gravity.

Demonic force shaped through Witch law.

The ruler’s knees hit stone.

Elias tore free.

His claws entered the broken breastplate Zee had already opened.

The Demon ruler caught his arm.

Elias’s bones cracked.

His face tightened.

Then his Demon strength answered.

Not enough to overpower.

Enough to hold.

His Witch side saw the wound.

His Demon side supplied the force.

Together.

Elias drove deeper.

The ruler gasped.

Elias whispered:

“You do not own what survived you.”

Then ripped out the heart.

The Demon ruler fell.

The remaining Demons felt it.

Some stopped.

Some fled.

Some fought harder.

Darkheart killed the ones who continued attacking.

The rest escaped east.

Zee let them.

They had seen enough.

⸻

Elias stood over the body.

Bleeding.

Shaking.

Alive.

Zee approached.

“You good?”

“No.”

“Excellent.”

Elias laughed once.

Then winced.

“You have gotten worse at comfort.”

“I was never good.”

“That is true.”

Ner reached them.

Zee immediately listened.

Two heartbeats.

Ner stared.

“Do not start.”

“I did nothing.”

“You made the face.”

“What face?”

“The heartbeat face.”

Elias looked between them.

“You have a heartbeat face?”

“Yes,” Ner said.

“No,” Zee said.

Zayrlen kicked.

All three felt the small surge of Crimson and Gold magic.

Elias froze.

Then looked at Ner.

“That was him?”

“Yes.”

For the first time since his rescue, the black edge in Elias’s expression softened completely.

“Can I?”

Ner considered.

Then nodded.

Elias placed one hand carefully against Ner.

Zayrlen moved again.

Elias laughed.

Not bitter.

Not exhausted.

The old laugh.

The one Zee remembered from years before the Hollow Crown.

“There you are.”

Ner looked at him.

“You have not met him.”

“I was talking to myself.”

“Concerning.”

“Very.”

Zee watched Elias.

Alive.

Changed.

Family.

Still himself.

The Order had not created Elias Marr.

They had only injured him.

Zee had given his oldest friend enough new blood to survive what they did.

The distinction mattered.

It always would.

⸻

Chapter One Hundred Fifteen

The Eighth Month

Darkheart buried five people after the Demon attack.

Three soldiers.

One Wolf scout.

One Witch healer.

No children.

That mattered.

It did not make the five smaller.

Zee stood through every burial.

Elias stood beside him.

Not behind.

The Demon–Witch scars remained visible along his throat.

His original deep-blue Mana occasionally flickered beneath his skin when emotion rose.

Nobody in Darkheart stared anymore.

That took less than a week.

Darkheart had become difficult to impress.

⸻

Elias returned to his old rooms.

They were exactly as he left them.

Mostly.

Rez had stolen two books.

Zareth had broken a chair.

Kael denied eating the emergency food.

Ner had apparently stored three boxes inside without asking.

Elias stood in the doorway.

“This is disrespectful.”

Zee leaned against the wall.

“You were missing.”

“That does not make my room public property.”

“It apparently did.”

Elias looked at the broken chair.

“Zareth.”

“Yes.”

“How?”

“He sat down.”

Elias stared.

“He can control his strength.”

“Usually.”

“I hate all of you.”

“Good.”

Elias entered.

His fingers brushed the old desk.

There were knife marks in one corner.

He remembered making them at sixteen because Zee had dared him to stab a moving target while blindfolded.

A shelf still held one of Aurelia’s old spellbooks.

Not important enough for royal archives.

Important enough for Elias to keep.

He touched the spine.

Then stopped.

Zee did not say anything.

Neither did Elias.

Aurelia remained dead.

Memory did not require resurrection.

After a moment, Elias asked:

“Did you think I was dead?”

“Yes.”

“How long?”

“Six weeks.”

“That was not what I asked.”

Zee looked at him.

Elias understood.

Every day.

Zee had thought it possible every day.

Elias sat on the edge of the bed.

“They changed my scent.”

“Yes.”

“My Mana.”

“Yes.”

“My blood.”

“Yes.”

“You still came.”

“Ner found the prisoners.”

Elias smiled faintly.

“Of course he did.”

Zee looked toward the floor.

“I should have found you sooner.”

Elias’s expression changed.

“No.”

Zee looked up.

“I was escorting Darkheart families.”

“Yes.”

“They survived.”

“Yes.”

“I did my job.”

“And you were taken.”

“That was their choice.”

Zee said nothing.

Elias leaned back.

“Do not make yourself responsible for every cage in the world just because you can break most of them.”

Zee smiled faintly.

“That sounded annoyingly reasonable.”

“I have been friends with you for too long.”

There.

No retelling needed.

No grand correction.

Elias had belonged here long before Demon blood entered him.

And he remained here now.

⸻

Ner entered the eighth month during a thunderstorm.

Zee knew before Tessa confirmed anything.

Zayrlen’s heartbeat changed.

Again.

Not weaker.

Heavier.

The unborn child’s Dragon nature had begun responding to pressure in the sky.

Every thunderclap made the heartbeat accelerate.

Every flash of lightning caused faint Crimson-and-Gold Witch patterns to move beneath Ner’s skin.

The Wolf rhythm remained strongest at night.

Dragon heat strongest during storms.

Witch resonance strongest around Ner.

Not Ner’s exact Pure Gold Mana.

Zayrlen’s own developing magic carried both fathers visibly.

Crimson.

Gold.

One expression.

Ner stood on the balcony during the storm.

Zee found him there.

“You are wet.”

“I noticed.”

“Come inside.”

“No.”

“Ner.”

“I like the rain.”

Zee looked at the lightning.

“You are carrying a child with Dragon blood.”

“Yes.”

“Standing outside during a magical thunderstorm.”

“Yes.”

“That seems irresponsible.”

Ner turned.

“You murdered an entire Phoenix kingdom and came home with wings.”

“That was different.”

“How?”

“I was not pregnant.”

Ner stared.

Zee realized he had lost the argument.

Zayrlen moved.

A pulse of heat rolled from Ner.

The rain around his body turned briefly to steam.

Both men froze.

Ner looked down.

“Well.”

Zee stepped closer.

Another thunderclap.

Crimson-and-Gold energy moved.

A Wolf-shaped pressure briefly appeared behind Ner.

Not a transformation.

Not even a complete projection.

Instinct.

Four-legged.

Low.

Protective.

Then gone.

Zee’s Wolf nature responded immediately.

He looked toward the place it had been.

Ner watched him.

“What?”

“He is going to have a true Wolf form.”

Ner smiled.

“You sound surprised.”

“I am not.”

“You are.”

“Only by the color.”

“What color?”

Zee looked deeper.

The developing Wolf pressure had not resembled his own near-black Wolf.

Not even close.

Crimson dominated the outline.

Gold moved through it.

Both fathers.

Zee touched Ner.

“He is going to be Crimson and Gold.”

Ner went quiet.

His hand covered Zee’s.

“Both of us.”

“Yes.”

The rain kept falling.

Zee smiled.

That particular inheritance felt right.

⸻

The first real pregnancy complication arrived twelve days later.

Not labor.

Power.

Ner collapsed during council.

One second he was insulting a trade proposal.

The next, Pure Gold Mana exploded from his body.

The entire chamber went bright.

Zee was across the table before Ner hit the ground.

Phoenix wings blocked everyone else instinctively.

“Ner.”

“I am awake.”

Good.

Zee listened.

Ner’s heartbeat.

Fast.

Zayrlen’s.

Faster.

Too fast.

Tessa pushed past Zee’s wing.

“Move.”

“No.”

“Move or I remove it.”

Zee moved.

Tessa knelt.

Gold-white healing light passed over Ner.

Then recoiled.

Not injury.

Overload.

“What?”

Tessa looked at the magic moving beneath Ner’s skin.

“He is drawing too much.”

Ner breathed through the pressure.

“Who?”

Zee stared.

“Zayrlen.”

The unborn child’s Witch foundation had latched onto Ner’s Pure Gold Mana.

Not stealing it.

Using it as the nearest structure to develop against.

Too aggressively.

Ner’s own magic kept answering.

Parent feeding child.

Instinctively.

And if it continued—

Ner would burn himself empty.

Zee’s face hardened.

“Can you stop it?”

Tessa shook her head.

“Not without disrupting the pregnancy.”

Ner grabbed Zee’s wrist.

“Do not touch his nature.”

“I was not going to.”

“You were thinking about it.”

“I think about many things.”

“Badly.”

Even now.

Good.

Zee placed his hand over Ner.

Crimson Sovereign senses opened completely.

Witch.

Vampire.

Wolf.

Then Dragon.

Phoenix.

He could feel the child.

Zayrlen was not attacking Ner.

He did not know how.

The developing Witch nature had simply found Pure Gold Mana and recognized:

Father.

Source.

Safety.

It kept reaching.

Zee closed his eyes.

Then fed something else into the space.

Not Vampire.

Never.

Not Phoenix.

Not Demon.

Those did not belong to Zayrlen.

Dragon first.

His own inherited Veyrath blood.

Heat entered gently.

Zayrlen reacted.

The pull on Ner’s Mana weakened.

Then Zee added Witch resonance.

Crimson.

Not creating a new nature.

The Witch nature already belonged to their son by birth.

Zee simply gave it another parent to recognize.

Crimson met Gold.

Zayrlen’s heartbeat slowed.

Ner’s Mana stopped flooding outward.

Silence.

Then—

a tiny magical pulse moved back through Zee’s hand.

Crimson.

Gold.

Zee opened his eyes.

Ner looked at him.

“Did he just push you?”

“Yes.”

Ner smiled weakly.

“Good.”

Zee stared.

“Why good?”

“Because you needed it.”

Tessa sighed.

“He is definitely yours.”

⸻

The incident changed the pregnancy.

After that, Zee regularly fed controlled Witch resonance into Zayrlen’s developing magic.

Not power.

Not an awakening.

Balance.

Two fathers.

Two magical patterns.

Ner’s Pure Gold.

Zee’s Crimson Witch structure.

Zayrlen settled between them.

The child’s own Mana remained uniquely his.

Crimson and Gold.

Neither father erased.

Neither copied exactly.

Except for the things meant to pass cleanly.

Dragon blood.

Wolf instinct.

Witch nature.

Their son was becoming himself before either could meet him.

⸻

Zareth arrived two days after hearing Ner had collapsed.

He entered in human form.

No joke.

No sarcasm.

“Is he safe?”

Ner nodded.

“Yes.”

“And Zayrlen?”

“Yes.”

Only then did Zareth relax.

His gaze moved toward Zee.

You nearly lost your mind.

No.

Liar.

Zee ignored him.

Elias entered carrying food.

Rez arrived from Vesper before dinner.

Kael.

Tessa.

Amara.

Rhyven.

No council had been called.

They simply came.

Family did that.

Elias set food down.

Ner looked at the tray.

“I am not dying.”

Tessa responded immediately.

“You are eating.”

“I already ate.”

“When?”

Ner paused.

Tessa pointed toward the food.

“Exactly.”

Rez sat beside him.

“Do what she says.”

Ner looked offended.

“You are the worst person here.”

Zareth looked toward Zee.

“Debatable.”

Rhyven quietly stole food from the edge of the tray.

Amara slapped his hand.

Kael took the same piece while they argued.

Elias watched all of them.

Then laughed.

Zee looked around the room.

Chosen family.

Old blood.

New blood.

Natural Tribrids.

Created Tribrids.

Hybrids that had never existed before.

People who remained exactly what they had always been.

Nobody mattered more because they had more races inside them.

That law had to remain.

Power changed bodies.

It did not decide family.

⸻

Then Zayrlen kicked hard enough for Ner to flinch.

Everyone stopped.

Ner stared around the room.

“No.”

Rez smiled.

“No what?”

“No one is touching me.”

Zareth raised his hand.

“I was not—”

“You absolutely were.”

Elias smiled.

“May I?”

Ner considered.

Then nodded.

Elias went first because he had nearly died before getting the chance.

He placed one hand against Ner.

Zayrlen moved.

Elias smiled.

“Strong.”

Kael received permission next.

Then Tessa.

Amara.

Rhyven hesitated at the edge of the room.

Ner noticed.

“You too.”

Rhyven blinked.

“I am not family.”

Silence.

Zee looked at him.

Rhyven realized his mistake.

Amara crossed her arms.

“You live here.”

Kael added:

“You fight here.”

Elias said:

“You steal food here.”

Rhyven looked at the bread in his hand.

Rez smiled.

“Unfortunately, that qualifies.”

Rhyven looked toward Zee.

Zee shrugged.

“Darkheart has low standards.”

Ner laughed.

Then held out his hand.

Rhyven approached.

Carefully.

His palm touched Ner.

Zayrlen moved.

Crimson Phoenix heat inside Rhyven reacted—

then immediately quieted.

Not compatible.

Not part of the child.

Zayrlen’s developing nature recognized something foreign and ignored it.

Rhyven smiled faintly.

“He does not like me.”

Zee listened.

“No.”

Rhyven looked up.

Zee’s smile appeared.

“He does not know you yet.”

Different.

Rhyven nodded.

He could live with that.

⸻

Later, when everyone finally left, Zee lay beside Ner.

One Phoenix wing covered both of them.

Ner rested against his chest.

Zayrlen’s heartbeat filled the quiet.

Eighth month.

Alive.

Strong.

Growing.

Ner spoke into the darkness.

“You know he is going to be trouble.”

“Yes.”

“You sound proud.”

“Yes.”

“He is going to break things.”

“Yes.”

“Probably bite someone.”

“Definitely.”

Ner smiled.

Then became quiet.

“He gets to know us.”

Zee’s expression changed.

“Yes.”

“Both of us.”

“Yes.”

“No hiding.”

“No.”

“No pretending.”

“No.”

Ner took Zee’s hand and placed it over their son.

Zayrlen pushed back.

Zee smiled in the dark.

For once, the future did not feel like something he needed to erase before it arrived.

It felt like someone he was waiting to meet.

Chapter One Hundred Sixteen

The Birth of the Crimson-Gold Prince

Zayrlen chose the middle of the night.

Of course he did.

Ner woke Zee by grabbing one of his horns.

Hard.

Chapter One Hundred Seventeen

Chapter One Hundred Twenty

The Prince Who Stayed in the Light

The morning after the kidnapping attempt, Darkheart expected Zee to disappear his son.

No illusion changing his face.

Still recovering.

Still armed.

Still capable of killing anyone stupid enough to mistake recovery for weakness.

Zareth leaned against one column in Human form.

Not arranged like guards.

“Majesty.”

Silence.

Different.

Its walls.

Its names.

Agreement.

Not discussion.

Already decided.

Too believable.

A Wolf.

Mostly.

Crimson-Gold.

With him.

Suppressed scent.

Hidden Witch signatures.

Magic behaving too quietly.

His Witchcraft.

His race.

His expression.

You are unreasonable.

Chapter One Hundred Twenty-Two

The Forest That Silenced Blood

The trees bent toward Zee and Rez.

There was none.

Every trunk leaned.

Every branch angled inward.

Then stabilized.

Enough to matter.

Zareth arrived through the balcony in Human form before anyone called.

His face was already wrong.

“The Link is fading.”

Silence.

Ner looked at him.

“What does that mean?”

“I can still feel Zee.”

Zareth’s Teal-and-Gold Mana flickered.

“But less.”

Rez’s location.

Vesper.

Everyone understood.

Ner handed Zayrlen to Elias.

Elias blinked.

“What are you doing?”

“Going.”

“No.”

Ner looked at him.

Elias continued quickly.

“I mean—absolutely not alone.”

Amara entered behind him.

“Already coming.”

Kael appeared from the hall.

“So am I.”

Rhyven arrived next.

Tessa last.

Zayrlen screamed again.

Zareth’s expression became lethal.

“Move.”

Back in Vesper, Zee felt the forest push deeper.

Witchcraft dimmed again.

Wolf instinct went quiet.

Vampire senses collapsed to almost Human range.

Dragon blood cooled.

Phoenix fire disappeared entirely.

For the first time in years—

Zee felt small.

Not powerless.

But reduced.

The hollow creature noticed.

Its fingers closed around Zee’s throat.

Rez attacked from behind.

The creature released Zee and struck him instead.

Rez’s Vampire speed failed halfway through the dodge.

The blow caught his ribs.

He flew.

Zee heard the crack.

Something inside him changed.

Not power.

Decision.

He could not overpower the forest as himself.

So he stopped trying.

Zee looked at the creature.

Human heartbeat absent.

No blood.

No scent.

No Mana.

No supernatural core.

But it still occupied space.

Still moved air.

Still had weight.

Still bent branches.

Assassin training answered.

Not bloodline.

Skill.

Zee watched the shoulders.

Hip rotation.

Foot placement.

Balance.

The creature lunged.

Zee stepped aside.

Human speed.

Perfect timing.

He caught the elbow.

Turned.

Used momentum.

The creature hit the ground.

Zee drove his knee into the shoulder joint.

Bone snapped.

The creature reacted.

Good.

Physical anatomy.

Different.

But present.

Zee smiled.

“There you are.”

⸻

Rez rose slowly.

“You look happy.”

“I found something it cannot suppress.”

“What?”

“Practice.”

Rez smiled.

“Finally useful.”

Its leg struck Zee’s chest.

Then rolled.

Stood.

No supernatural flourish.

No flight.

No spells.

Just Nanda Parbat.

Angles.

Breath.

Joint destruction.

Momentum.

Pressure.

He fought like the assassin he had trained to become.

The creature adapted.

So did he.

It reached.

He broke fingers.

It kicked.

He took the leg.

Twisted the knee.

It tried using the hollow chest to release suppression directly.

Zee jammed a broken branch through the cavity.

The creature froze.

Rez stared.

“That worked?”

Zee did too.

Then smiled.

“Apparently.”

Blue-White Mana returned slightly around Rez.

The forest shuddered.

The creature had been part of the suppression network.

Not the source.

But an anchor.

Zee drove the branch deeper.

The hollow body cracked from inside.

Then collapsed into gray ash.

The forest screamed.

Every tree bent away.

Zee’s powers returned at once.

Not fully.

Enough.

Phoenix fire ignited.

Crimson wings erupted.

Vampire hearing flooded back.

Wolf scent returned.

Witchcraft sharpened.

Dragon heat roared beneath his scales.

The Crimson Sovereign snapped into complete alignment.

Rez looked at him.

“There he is.”

Zee’s eyes became Crimson-Gold.

“No.”

He looked deeper into the forest.

“Now I am angry.”

⸻

The surviving villagers behind Rez’s barrier began recovering.

Slowly.

A Wolf shifted accidentally.

A Vampire’s wound started closing.

Witches felt Mana return in weak pulses.

The suppression had not permanently stripped them.

Good.

Zee looked toward the ashes.

Then farther into the trees.

“How many anchors?”

Rez closed his eyes.

His Blue-White Mana spread carefully.

“More than one.”

Zee’s Wolf scent found nothing.

Blood Mark had nothing.

The King’s Hunt had no biological prey.

So he used the one thing the forest could not erase.

Pattern.

The trees bent toward active anchors.

Not randomly.

Directionally.

Then pointed northeast.

“There.”

Rez frowned.

“How?”

“They lean.”

Rez looked.

Then smiled.

“Very annoying.”

“Yes.”

They moved.

⸻

The second anchor died faster.

The third fought harder.

By the fourth, the forest understood Zee had learned.

So it changed.

Suppression no longer attacked all his bloodlines equally.

Then Phoenix.

Then Wolf.

Trying different order.

Zee noticed.

“So you learn.”

The voice answered.

Yes.

“Good.”

Rez looked at him.

“Why is that good?”

Zee smiled.

“Because now I know it is choosing.”

Choice meant responsibility.

Responsibility meant prey.

⸻

They found the center before midnight.

Not a creature.

A tree.

Ancient.

Larger than any living tree in Vesper.

Its roots spread beneath all three affected villages.

Its trunk was pale.

No leaves.

No bark.

The surface looked like bone.

Hundreds of hollow creatures were embedded inside it.

Sleeping.

Or waiting.

Human.

An old woman in gray robes.

“You killed four children.”

Rez’s expression changed.

Zee did not.

“The hollow ones?”

“They are extensions.”

“Yours?”

“Yes.”

“I corrected imbalance.”

Zee’s eyes narrowed.

“What imbalance?”

“You.”

There it was.

“Creation has accelerated.”

Phoenix–Wolf.

Phoenix–Dragon–Witch.

Demon–Witch.

Natural Tribrid Prince.

New bloodlines.

Old boundaries collapsing.

The woman did not.

Suppression slammed outward.

Zee’s wings extinguished.

Again.

Plain steel.

Zee stepped forward.

“I have killed people without magic before.”

Chapter One Hundred Twenty-Three

The Thing That Could Not Silence Choice

The old woman raised one hand.

The forest swallowed sound.

Something different.

A dead zone.

No spell words.

No Dragon roar.

Plain.

Sharp.

Rez understood.

No powers.

Fine.

They had both survived worse.

The hollow creatures attacked.

⸻

Efficient.

No wasted movement.

Steel through joints.

Knees broken.

Throats cut even when no blood came.

Faster.

More surgical.

Not supernatural speed.

Skill.

Knife through elbow.

Turn.

Blade beneath jaw.

Twist.

Kicked backward.

Broke a knee.

“You should be helpless.”

I was born helpless once.

Good.

The tree opened.

Not physically at first.

The suppression deepened.

Then Witch.

Wolf.

Dragon.

Phoenix.

No claws.

No fire.

No supernatural strength.

His face changed.

Red.

Ordinary-looking.

“You see?”

Then grabbed the blade.

His heart kept beating.

Weakly.

But beating.

Her eyes widened.

Immortality remained.

Not as an active bloodline.

As fact.

Death had already ended once.

The forest could suppress expression.

Not rewrite history.

Hard.

She staggered.

Rez laughed despite himself.

The sound still did not carry.

Bad idea for anyone else.

Slow.

Painful.

Good.

The woman was trained.

Not enough.

No dignity.

No ceremony.

Survival.

The suppression flickered.

One heartbeat of Wolf returned.

Enough.

Blood Mark locked.

Gone.

Interesting.

Hundreds.

“Good.”

Choice.

Tree or brother.

Brother.

Heel into another spine.

Hands tearing.

Ripped.

“No.”

“Yes.”

True Dragon form.

Huge.

His Phoenix fire extinguished.

Witch sigils vanished.

Dragon strength weakened.

Not gone.

Zee.

Do not enter.

Too late.

Stood.

No Phoenix.

Good enough.

His Demon–Witch magic failed at the boundary.

Kael followed.

Vampire side gone.

Wolf gone.

No healer glow.

No magic.

“Obviously.”

Family.

Not because of power.

Not because of bloodlines.

Because they chose to enter the place where all those things could be taken away.

For him.

That mattered more than any new race.

⸻

Far away in Darkheart, Ner held Zayrlen.

The baby had stopped crying.

Because something else had stabilized.

The pack signal around him changed.

Ner felt it.

Not fear now.

Recognition.

Many.

Family moving toward father.

Crimson-Gold eyes.

“Of course they did.”

Inside the suppression forest, power meant nothing.

So the fight became honest.

Kael fought with a sword.

Amara with knives.

Tessa dragged wounded people out of the pile and treated them without magic.

Rez held the left flank.

Family blood.

“No.”

Elias understood.

“Ordinary fire.”

“Yes.”

Good.

Oil from abandoned supply packs.

Cloth.

Flint.

Human fire.

The tree screamed.

Suppression weakened.

One percent.

Enough.

Zee’s Vampire healing flickered.

His heart wound began closing.

The woman stared.

“No.”

Wolf returned.

Then Witch.

Then Dragon heat.

Then Phoenix.

Crimson Sovereign synchronization snapped back piece by piece.

Zee opened his eyes.

Crimson-Gold.

The woman backed away.

“No.”

His Phoenix wings erupted behind him.

Huge.

Crimson.

Black-edged.

Burning.

Zareth’s Dragon nature exploded back next.

He shifted.

True Dragon form filled the clearing.

Teal-and-Gold scales.

Phoenix fire.

Witch sigils.

Elias’s blue-black Demon-Witch Mana returned.

Rhyven dropped into true Wolf form as Crimson fire burst through his claws.

Amara shifted beside him.

Kael vanished in Vampire speed.

Rez’s Blue-White Mana flooded the forest.

The pale tree had made one mistake.

It taught them exactly what they were without power.

Then gave the power back.

The old woman ran.

Blood Mark found her immediately.

The King’s Hunt now had identity.

Wolf scent caught her fear.

Vampire hearing found the heartbeat.

Witchcraft read the escape ward.

Phoenix wings made distance meaningless.

Dragon force broke the trees between.

“You do not understand.”

“No.”

“To preserve balance.”

“You suppressed children.”

“To preserve the world.”

Zee’s expression became flat.

“That sounds like your choice.”

Too late.

“Wait.”

Zee did not.

She died.

No surrender.

No second chance.

She had knowingly attacked Vesper citizens and stripped supernatural natures from entire villages.

Confirmed.

Enough.

⸻

The pale tree came next.

Zareth attacked from above.

Dragonfire hit the upper trunk.

Phoenix renewal twisted strangely through it, making the fire sustain itself.

Elias used Demon-Witch sigils to bind the roots in place.

Rez’s Blue-White Mana prevented the suppression pulse from rebuilding.

Rhyven burned the lower roots.

Amara hunted the hollow creatures escaping the trunk.

Kael destroyed each exposed anchor.

Tessa stayed with the wounded.

Zee flew straight into the center.

Phoenix wings shielding.

Dragon force driving him through pale wood.

Witch sight finding the internal structure.

There.

A knot.

Not a heart.

Not blood.

A vacancy.

An intentional absence around which the entire network had been built.

“Sever.”

The tree resisted.

Ancient.

Exactly the kind of magic Spell Sever could not casually destroy.

Zee pushed harder.

The knot cracked.

Not enough.

He added Witch precision.

Dragon force.

Phoenix flame.

Crimson Sovereign fully mastered beneath all of it.

Not one giant attack.

Synchronization.

Each nature doing its part.

Wolf instinct told him where resistance shifted.

Vampire senses caught the tiniest returning pulses around the roots.

Witchcraft cut seams.

Dragon strength held the opening.

Phoenix flame prevented regrowth.

“Sever.”

The knot broke.

The tree died.

Every affected village felt it.

Witches collapsed as their magic came rushing back.

Vampires healed.

Wolves shifted.

Children with supernatural blood started crying from the sudden return of sensation.

Rez stood in the burning clearing.

Blue-White Mana strong again.

He looked toward Zee.

“Permanent?”

Zee listened.

“No.”

Good.

No stolen bloodlines.

No ruined generations.

The forest had suppressed.

Not erased.

Zee looked toward the dead pale tree.

The Age of New Blood had produced another enemy.

Not one that wanted to steal his power.

Not one that wanted to imitate him.

One that wanted to stop supernatural change entirely.

It had failed.

And it was dead.

Arc over.

⸻

They returned to Darkheart the following evening.

Ner waited in the courtyard with Zayrlen.

The moment Zee landed, the baby’s heartbeat changed.

Zee heard it from across the stone.

His wings folded.

He walked forward.

Not King.

Father.

Again.

Ner handed Zayrlen to him.

No words.

Zee took his son.

The baby settled immediately.

One tiny hand closed around Zee’s collar.

Zee touched his head.

“I am fine.”

“You were stabbed through the heart.”

Rez answered from behind him.

“He was being dramatic.”

Zee looked back.

“You were there.”

“Yes.”

“You were also injured.”

“Less dramatically.”

Ner sighed.

Crimson-Gold.

Slit for one heartbeat.

Then round.

A tiny patch of Crimson-and-Gold scales appeared across his shoulder.

Zee watched them fade.

Not fear.

Not distress.

Recognition.

His Dragon blood had reacted to Zee’s return.

The baby’s Wolf instincts had found pack.

His Witch pressure settled.

Zee smiled.

The world could suppress power.

Hide blood.

Build cages.

Silence magic.

Erase scent.

Mask heartbeats.

Create absence.

None of that changed the one thing Zee had learned beneath the pale tree.

Power was not what made Darkheart dangerous.

Choice was.

And surrounded by the people who had crossed into a forest stripped of every supernatural advantage simply because Zee was inside—

Zayrlen Keal Darkheart had been born into one of the most dangerous things in the world.

A family that came when called.

Chapter One Hundred Twenty-Four

The Blood That Chose Its Own Shape

Zayrlen developed a habit of waking before sunrise.

Not crying.

Watching.

Zee discovered this on the third morning after returning from Vesper.

He entered the nursery quietly.

Zayrlen was already awake.

Crimson-Gold eyes followed him across the room.

No sound.

No movement except one tiny hand opening and closing against the blanket.

Zee stopped beside the cradle.

“You are supposed to be asleep.”

Zayrlen stared.

Zee stared back.

The baby blinked.

Then a tiny patch of Crimson-and-Gold scales appeared along his temple.

Gone.

“Terrible argument.”

“You are debating a newborn again.”

“He started it.”

“He cannot speak.”

“That has not stopped him.”

Wolf recognition.

Pack.

No fear.

Public child.

Loved without concealment.

“Fine.”

“Progress.”

Darkheart’s defenses had become aggressive enough to annoy its own citizens.

“The ward is correct.”

“What?”

That never lasted.

The first indication came from Rhyven.

He was patrolling the western forest when his Phoenix-Wolf nature reacted to something underground.

Not danger.

Heat.

He stopped.

His claws ignited.

Then extinguished.

“What?”

Placed one hand against the soil.

“Something is warm.”

“No.”

“Magic?”

“Maybe.”

Wolf senses opened.

She smelled nothing unusual.

Heat moving beneath the earth in deliberate lines.

Not lava.

Not fire.

Something traveling.

He stood.

“It is going toward Darkheart.”

Amara’s expression changed.

“Call Zee.”

Phoenix blood recognized it immediately.

Not Phoenix.

Something adjacent.

Artificial heat.

Contained.

Moving through stone.

Zee’s Witch sight opened.

There.

A narrow line beneath the soil.

Runes.

Not attacking.

Transporting something.

Kael arrived next.

Then Elias.

Zareth landed in Human form.

Rez was still in Vesper.

Ner remained at the keep with Zayrlen.

For now.

Zee crouched.

“Someone built another route beneath us.”

Amara frowned.

“Not another tunnel.”

“No.”

Elias studied the runes.

“A spellway.”

Zee looked toward him.

“Old?”

“Yes.”

“Older than Darkheart’s current borders.”

Good.

Not another enemy who had built beneath them yesterday without detection.

Kingdom progression had simply reached it.

His Witch senses reacted.

Then his Dragon side.

“Something living traveled through here.”

“What?”

“Not sure.”

Rhyven’s Phoenix heat surged again.

Not loud.

Deep.

“Dragon.”

Zee looked at him.

“Drakonis?”

“No.”

“Veyrath?”

Zareth listened.

“No.”

Another Dragon bloodline.

Ancient.

Independent.

Good.

Dragon.

Blood.

Wolf.

Amara noticed.

One Dragon.

One Wolf.

Badly.

Phoenix wings carried him through the shaft.

a Dragon lay in Human form.

Female.

Dark copper skin.

Black hair.

One horn broken.

a Wolf man.

Barely conscious.

Two heartbeats.

Weak.

Saw Zee’s horns.

Saw Zareth.

“Not them.”

“Who?”

Failed.

Again?

“Not blood.”

Different.

Good.

Silence.

Zareth’s expression changed.

Dragon Link.

The Dragon woman saw it.

Zee’s pupils narrowed.

“Yes.”

“A soul-link.”

Because that sounded too close to something neither wanted casually named by strangers.

“Rare. Natural. Cannot be manufactured correctly.”

Good.

“People have been trying.”

Worse.

Ner came too.

With Zayrlen.

Ner stared.

“Do not.”

“There are injured strangers with unknown bloodlines.”

“Yes.”

“Yes.”

“Why?”

“Because Tessa needed my Bloodsong to stabilize one of them.”

Zee looked at the Wolf.

His heartbeat was collapsing.

Ner was right.

Annoying.

Again.

He handed Zayrlen to Elias.

Elias blinked.

“Why me?”

“Because your hands are clean.”

“That is disturbingly rare.”

Zee ignored him.

Ner knelt beside the Wolf.

Pure Gold Mana opened.

Bloodsong reached into the damaged rhythm.

The heartbeat steadied.

Barely.

Tessa worked.

The Dragon woman watched Zayrlen.

Her eyes widened.

“What is that child?”

She noticed.

Good.

Ner answered first.

“Our son.”

Then Zayrlen.

Dragon.

Witch.

Wolf.

Natural.

“They will come for him.”

Zee’s expression flattened.

“Who?”

“The Bond Collectors.”

“That is a terrible name.”

Elias muttered:

“Agreed.”

“They do not take bloodlines.”

“What do they take?”

“Relationships.”

Ner’s expression changed.

The woman looked at Zee and Zareth.

“They find rare supernatural bonds. Dragon Links. Pack-binding. Witch soul-pacts. Bloodsong resonance. Sire connections.”

Rez was absent.

Aidan.

Uncle Rez.

Memory.

No.

Not relevant.

Not exposed.

He pushed it aside.

“They cut the bond out of one person and force it into another.”

Zareth’s face became murderous.

Zee’s wings opened.

Crimson fire moved.

That was enough explanation.

⸻

The collectors arrived before sunset.

Fast.

Too fast.

Meaning they had been tracking the survivors.

Not Darkheart.

Good.

Independent event.

No conspiracy swallowing everything.

No banner.

No masks.

No attempt at diplomacy.

“There.”

Bad.

He could perceive it.

“Leave.”

“Zee Darkheart.”

“Yes.”

“We only want what belongs to us.”

“They do not.”

“Severed from whom?”

“My brother.”

Silence.

The collector smiled.

“He died.”

Her face broke for half a second.

Then hardened.

“And you kept the link.”

“Part of it.”

The spellway.

The heat.

The suffering.

Not blood.

Not race.

A relationship made supernatural.

Disgusting in a new direction.

Zee killed him.

Immediately.

The other four attacked.

⸻

One hook struck toward Zareth.

Then something tried pulling.

Not flesh.

Link.

His eyes changed.

Zareth felt it too.

Rage struck through the Link.

They touched it.

Zee’s answer came colder.

I know.

The hook tried extracting the connection.

The Dragon Link stretched.

Not broke.

The collector holding the other end screamed.

Zee pulled him forward.

Dragon strength.

Vampire speed.

Wolf aggression.

Witch precision.

Teal-and-Gold scales.

Witch sigils.

No mercy.

Wrong family.

Ner protected the survivors.

And Zayrlen.

“Down.”

Ended him.

Wolf speed.

Phoenix-Wolf fire.

Plural.

“Yes.”

Crimson-Gold eyes.

Heat.

Something enormous waiting.

For three hours.

Again.

Zee stared.

“Was that—”

Zee smiled too.

Collectors hunted bonds.

Ancient forests suppressed supernatural life.

Darkheart kept expanding.

The world remained dangerous.

Inside the nursery—

⸻

Chapter One Hundred Twenty-Five

The First Time the Prince Left Darkheart

Zayrlen left Darkheart for the first time at two months old.

Zee hated the idea.

Which was exactly why Ner decided they were doing it.

“He cannot spend his entire infancy inside one kingdom.”

“He is two months old.”

“Yes.”

“He does not know what a kingdom is.”

“Then this will be educational.”

“He cannot hold his own head up for long.”

“Zee.”

“No.”

Ner stared.

Zee corrected immediately.

“I would prefer not.”

“Better.”

“Still no.”

Ner smiled.

“You do understand you are not winning.”

“Yes.”

That was the problem.

⸻

The destination was Vesper.

Safe.

Close.

Family.

Rez had been demanding a visit since the birth.

Demanding was generous.

Threatening was more accurate.

His last message had read:

If you do not bring my nephew soon, I am coming to collect him myself.

Zee had replied:

Try.

Rez responded:

I raised you better than this.

Completely false.

Still irritating.

So they went.

Ner carried Zayrlen.

Zee flew above part of the route.

He was.

Amara led a Wolf escort.

Kael rode near the rear.

Elias came because he claimed Vesper owed him replacement books.

Rhyven came because Rez had apparently promised him food.

Zareth joined midway through the route without invitation.

Naturally.

Zee looked at him.

“Why are you here?”

“I am traveling.”

“To Vesper.”

“Yes.”

“At the exact same time.”

“Yes.”

“To see Zayrlen.”

Zareth looked offended.

“That is speculative.”

Through the Link came:

Obviously.

Zee ignored him.

⸻

The road remained quiet.

No attack.

No hidden threat.

No kidnapping.

That itself felt suspicious.

Zee checked the tree line every few minutes.

Ner noticed.

“You are doing it again.”

“What?”

“Expecting the world to ruin something.”

Zee looked toward him.

Ner adjusted Zayrlen against his chest.

“He is allowed to have a boring trip.”

Zee looked at their son.

Zayrlen slept through the entire conversation.

“Boring feels irresponsible.”

Ner smiled.

“That might be the most Zee sentence you have ever said.”

⸻

Vesper saw them coming.

Mostly because Zee’s enormous Crimson Phoenix wings were difficult to miss.

Blue-White banners moved in the wind.

Rez stood in the courtyard before their horses fully stopped.

Did not greet Ner.

“Give him to me.”

Ner laughed.

Zee frowned.

“You could say hello.”

“Hello.”

Then at Ner.

“Hello.”

“Give him to me.”

Zee stared.

“That was fast.”

“You have had him for two months.”

“He is my son.”

Rez smiled.

“And my nephew.”

No hidden meaning spoken aloud.

No dangerous truth.

Just Zayrlen.

Crimson-Gold.

Then grabbed Rez’s coat.

Rez smiled.

“There he is.”

Zee’s expression shifted.

Something old moved quietly in his chest.

With another son.

Rez did.

That was enough.

Then he turned his attention fully to Zayrlen.

No comparison.

No stolen moment.

Good.

⸻

Vesper welcomed the Prince without ceremony.

Lucien was gone from the story’s active center now, but Vesper still carried the culture he had built.

Blue-White flame lit the central courtyard.

Children gathered.

Witches whispered.

More stared at Zayrlen.

“Is he dangerous?”

“Yes.”

Ner answered:

“He is a baby.”

The child looked confused.

Rez smiled.

“Both answers are correct.”

Zayrlen sneezed.

A tiny Crimson-and-Gold spark hit Rez’s shoulder.

The child laughed.

“Dangerous.”

Zee looked smug.

Ner gave up.

⸻

The important moment happened in the old Vesper gardens.

Rez carried Zayrlen beneath trees Zee remembered from childhood.

Zareth had disappeared somewhere with Elias and Kael.

Probably causing expensive damage.

Amara and Rhyven were arguing near the wall.

Zayrlen stared at the water.

Zee stopped too.

Water.

Aidan.

Great Vesper River.

Maternal inheritance.

A boy saying:

It knows me.

The memory hit sharply.

Rez felt Zee go still.

Ner noticed only the change in posture.

“What?”

Zee looked at the fountain.

“Nothing.”

Ner studied him.

Different from years ago.

He knew when not to push.

Rez turned slightly.

Zayrlen reached toward the water.

Nothing happened.

Good.

No Ocean.

No Abyss.

No Siren inheritance.

Different son.

Different blood.

The fountain remained ordinary.

Rez looked at Zee.

Zee nodded once.

The moment passed.

⸻

Then Zayrlen growled.

Tiny.

Ridiculous.

Unmistakable.

Ner looked at him.

“Was that a growl?”

Rez smiled.

“Yes.”

Zee stepped closer.

Zayrlen stared at a statue beside the fountain.

A carved Wolf.

His pupils narrowed.

Slit.

Tiny claws appeared.

Not distress.

Recognition.

The Vesper garden carried old Wolf scent from visiting allies.

Zayrlen reacted.

His true Wolf nature remained far from awakening.

But instinct was becoming more expressive.

Rez held him closer.

The growl stopped.

Zee looked at him.

“Do that again.”

Ner stared.

“He is not a performance.”

“I want to hear it.”

“He is two months old.”

“Still.”

Rez laughed.

Zayrlen immediately growled again.

Everyone stopped.

Rez looked smug.

Zee looked betrayed.

Ner laughed.

“Apparently he likes Uncle Rez.”

Zee folded his arms.

“Temporary.”

⸻

That evening, Vesper held dinner.

Nothing political.

Just family.

Zee kept watching him.

Finally Elias noticed.

“You are jealous.”

“No.”

“You are.”

“No.”

Kael looked toward Rez.

“He has been holding the baby for an hour.”

“One hour and twelve minutes,” Zee said.

Silence.

Elias smiled.

“You counted.”

“No.”

Zee regretted bringing any of them.

“He should visit Drakonis next.”

Zee answered immediately.

“No.”

Ner answered:

“Eventually.”

Zareth smiled.

Zee looked betrayed.

Again.

⸻

The attack came after dinner.

Not for Zayrlen.

Not for Zee.

Not for Vesper.

A meteor struck the western fields.

Actual meteor.

The impact shook the kingdom.

Every ward screamed.

Rez stood instantly.

Zayrlen woke and started crying.

Zee was beside him before the second tremor.

Ner took Zayrlen.

Rez’s Blue-White Mana filled the hall.

“What was that?”

Zareth’s Dragon senses reached farther.

His expression changed.

“Not stone.”

Zee looked toward him.

“What?”

“Alive.”

Silence.

Beyond the windows, something enormous moved inside the crater.

Not Demon.

Not Dragon.

Not Phoenix.

Not anything Zee recognized.

Good.

Rez handed control of the inner keep to Vesper guards.

Ner looked toward the crying baby.

Then at him.

“Go.”

No hesitation this time.

Progress.

Protected.

Known.

Loved.

⸻

The crater was enormous.

Black shell.

Six limbs.

Translucent sections showing blue light inside.

No recognizable blood.

No familiar Mana.

No scent Zee could classify.

Zareth stared.

“This is not from here.”

Rez looked toward the sky.

“Meaning?”

Zareth looked at Zee.

“Not this world.”

Silence.

Zee’s expression sharpened.

Beyond the stars.

The possibility had always existed.

Now something had landed in Vesper.

The creature rose.

Its shell unfolded.

Blue light spread across the field.

Zee’s Phoenix wings opened.

Crimson flame answered.

The creature looked directly at him.

Then spoke in a language none of them knew.

Except Elias.

His new Demon-Witch sigils reacted.

Not translation.

Pattern recognition.

He stared.

“What?”

Elias looked toward Zee.

“I think it asked what you are.”

Zee smiled.

Crimson-Gold eyes brightened.

“Tell it I am busy.”

Rez looked at him.

“You cannot be serious.”

The creature charged.

Zee launched.

“Apparently it understood.”

And for the first time in the Age of New Blood—

the danger coming toward Darkheart had not come from another kingdom.

It had come from beyond the world.
